literature.headline_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人乳头瘤病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在221名参与者中(女性占66.5%;平均年龄43.6岁(±13.9)),约有一半听说过HPV,而不到三分之一听说过HPV疫苗。教育水平是一个关键因素,教育程度较低的个体对HPV的认知显著较低(p < .000)。年龄(p < .033)、性别(p < .019)和教育水平(p < .004)预测了HPV疫苗的认知,女性、受教育程度较高者和年轻成年人更有可能听说过HPV疫苗。仅26.3%的年龄在26岁及以下的参与者接种过HPV疫苗。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0357586]
当应用于具有或不具有宫颈上皮内瘤变 2 或更严重 (CIN2+) 组织学 诊断 的临床样本时,该检测方法可靠地检测到了关键 HPV 基因型,但 234 个 HPV 阳性样本中的 7 个 (3%) 除外,所有样本都表现出非常低的病毒载量。 [10.1099/acmi.0.001166.v3]
然而,尽管一些非消融性干预措施已显示出治疗特定 人乳头瘤病毒 相关病变的功效,但尚无任何治疗方法能够证明在根除 人乳头瘤病毒 感染本身方面具有经证实且持久的功效。一些药物,包括免疫调节剂和儿茶素,被批准用于治疗外部肛门生殖器疣,但不能可靠地消除潜在的 人乳头瘤病毒 感染。 [10.1016/j.ijgc.2026.104950]
接种疫苗的意愿与感知的易感性、严重程度、行动线索、态度、感知的行为控制和主观规范相关。与汉族照顾者相比,回族照顾者的意愿较低,而高等教育、中等收入以及在党政机关或公共机构工作的人则预示着较高的意愿。感知到的障碍也与意愿呈正相关。 [10.1080/21645515.2026.2725492]

对于抗HPV-6/11/16/18/58 IgG,使用均值+3标准差[SD]和均值+5 SD阈值时,灵敏度和特异性均为100%。对于HPV-45,灵敏度在+3 SD阈值时为100%,在+5 SD阈值时为92.9%。在疫苗接种者中,IgA检测显示出中等阳性反应,其中在+3 SD阈值时,HPV-11的峰值估计为96.4%,HPV-58的峰值估计为85.7%。IgA与IgG呈正相关(Spearman's ρ = 0.74)。 [10.1002/jcla.70343]

literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Among the 221 participants (66.5% women; mean age 43.6 years (±13.9)), approximately half had heard of HPV, and fewer than one-third had heard of the HPV vaccine. Education emerged as a key factor, with individuals with lower educational attainment being significantly less aware of HPV (p < .000). [10.1371/journal.pone.0357586]

When applied to clinical samples with and without a histological diagnosis of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2 or worse (CIN2+), the assay reliably detected key HPV genotypes, with the exception of 7 of 234 (3%) of HPV-positive samples, all of which exhibited very low viral load. [10.1099/acmi.0.001166.v3]

However, no therapy has demonstrated proven and durable efficacy in eradicating human papillomavirus infection itself, although some non-ablative interventions have shown efficacy in treating specific human papillomavirus-related lesions. [10.1016/j.ijgc.2026.104950]
Willingness to vaccinate correlated with perceived susceptibility, severity, cues to action, attitudes, perceived behavioral control, and subjective norms. [10.1080/21645515.2026.2725492]

Overall, women with HPV infection had an increased risk of incident CVD (adjusted HR 1.07, 95% CI [1.05, 1.08], absolute rate difference 0.53 per 1,000 person-years, population-attributable fraction 1.16%) and CVD-related mortality (adjusted HR 1.25, 95% CI [1.16, 1.34], absolute rate difference 6.71 per 100,000 person-years, population-attributable fraction 4.12%) than those without. [10.1371/journal.pmed.1005222]

news.lead_zh: 本期人乳头瘤病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 事件是美国青少年HPV 疫苗接种率在过去四年中没有增加,如《发病率和死亡率周报》所报道。CDC作者指出,与其他常规青少年疫苗相比,HPV 疫苗接种接种覆盖率较低,可能是由于学校入学要求存在差异。 [news-42635ae0a2165876]
一项发表在《PLOS Medicine》上的研究指出,HPV感染可能略微增加女性新发心血管疾病(CVD)和死亡的风险,尤其是在随访的第一年内。 [news-939018155f88a7c6]
根据综合摘要,HPV 疫苗 被报告为与头颈癌风险降低 69% 相关,被描述为一种预防性癌症 治疗,现在很可能也保护男性。该条目是 RSS/综合摘要(内容状态:综合摘要);在提供的证据中未报告原始研究、作者、期刊、资助方、方法或确认状态。在该主题合同中,头颈癌在此上下文中被视为与 HPV 相关的口咽癌。 [news-671cf229040f4871]

news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Human papillomaviruses news developments.
key_findings_en: The event is the lack of increase in HPV vaccine uptake among US teenagers over the past four years, as reported in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. [news-42635ae0a2165876]

A research study published in PLOS Medicine suggests that HPV infection may confer a slightly higher risk of new-onset cardiovascular disease (CVD) and death, particularly within the first year of follow-up. [news-939018155f88a7c6]

According to the syndicated summary, the HPV vaccine is reported as being 'linked to a 69% lower risk of head and neck cancer,' described as a preventative cancer treatment now also likely protecting men. [news-671cf229040f4871]

papers.title: International Papillomavirus Society statement on reputed treatments for human papillomavirus infection and human papillomavirus-related diseases: evidence, risks, and standards for clinical evaluation
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus is the most common sexually transmitted infection and the necessary cause of cervical cancer, as well as a proportion of other anogenital and oropharyngeal cancers. Although most infections clear spontaneously, persistent oncogenic human papillomavirus infection may lead to precancer and cancer. There is therefore a need for effective and globally accessible therapies that either promote sustained clearance of human papillomavirus infection or safely treat human papillomavirus-related lesions, particularly in settings where ablative or excisional procedures are not readily available. However, no therapy has demonstrated proven and durable efficacy in eradicating human papillomavirus infection itself, although some non-ablative interventions have shown efficacy in treating specific human papillomavirus-related lesions. We conducted a narrative review of currently available and emerging interventions promoted for the treatment of human papillomavirus infection or human papillomavirus-related lesions, including approved topical agents, oral formulations, immunotherapies, therapeutic vaccines, molecular inhibitors, and widely marketed commercial products. Evidence was synthesized from clinical trials, systematic reviews, clinical guidelines, health technology assessments, and policy recommendations, and assessed using a structured evidence-evaluation framework. Some agents, including immune modulators and sinecatechins, are approved for external anogenital warts but do not reliably eliminate underlying human papillomavirus infection. Selected topical therapies, particularly 5-fluorouracil, have demonstrated efficacy in randomized trials for regression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia in specific clinical contexts, but do not represent validated antiviral eradication therapies. Photodynamic therapy, intralesional immunotherapy, therapeutic vaccines, and molecular inhibitors remain investigational, with insufficient evidence for routine clinical use. Probiotics, nutritional supplements, vaginal gels, and other commercially promoted products also lack robust evidence. In the absence of proven therapies that eradicate human papillomavirus infection, current management relies on surveillance, evidence-based treatment of precancerous lesions, vaccination, and screening. The proposed framework may support professional societies in evaluating emerging interventions and providing clear, evidence-based guidance to health care professionals, policymakers, patients, and the public.

papers.title_zh: 国际乳头瘤病毒协会关于著名的 人乳头瘤病毒 感染和 人乳头瘤病毒 相关疾病的声明:临床评估的证据、风险和标准
papers.source_body_en: Human papillomavirus is the most common sexually transmitted infection and the necessary cause of cervical cancer, as well as a proportion of other anogenital and oropharyngeal cancers. Although most infections clear spontaneously, persistent oncogenic human papillomavirus infection may lead to precancer and cancer. There is therefore a need for effective and globally accessible therapies that either promote sustained clearance of human papillomavirus infection or safely treat human papillomavirus-related lesions, particularly in settings where ablative or excisional procedures are not readily available. However, no therapy has demonstrated proven and durable efficacy in eradicating human papillomavirus infection itself, although some non-ablative interventions have shown efficacy in treating specific human papillomavirus-related lesions. We conducted a narrative review of currently available and emerging interventions promoted for the treatment of human papillomavirus infection or human papillomavirus-related lesions, including approved topical agents, oral formulations, immunotherapies, therapeutic vaccines, molecular inhibitors, and widely marketed commercial products. Evidence was synthesized from clinical trials, systematic reviews, clinical guidelines, health technology assessments, and policy recommendations, and assessed using a structured evidence-evaluation framework. Some agents, including immune modulators and sinecatechins, are approved for external anogenital warts but do not reliably eliminate underlying human papillomavirus infection. Selected topical therapies, particularly 5-fluorouracil, have demonstrated efficacy in randomized trials for regression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia in specific clinical contexts, but do not represent validated antiviral eradication therapies. Photodynamic therapy, intralesional immunotherapy, therapeutic vaccines, and molecular inhibitors remain investigational, with insufficient evidence for routine clinical use. Probiotics, nutritional supplements, vaginal gels, and other commercially promoted products also lack robust evidence. In the absence of proven therapies that eradicate human papillomavirus infection, current management relies on surveillance, evidence-based treatment of precancerous lesions, vaccination, and screening. The proposed framework may support professional societies in evaluating emerging interventions and providing clear, evidence-based guidance to health care professionals, policymakers, patients, and the public.

papers.title: Guardians’ willingness to vaccinate primary and secondary school girls against human papillomavirus and associated factors in ethnic autonomous prefectures of Qinghai Province, China: A cross-sectional study based on the Health Belief Model and Theory of Planned Behavior
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer is a preventable threat to women's health, and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is key primary prevention. Caregiver hesitancy may affect vaccination of age-eligible girls.We examined caregivers' willingness to vaccinate primary and secondary school girls against HPV and factors in six ethnic autonomous prefectures of Qinghai Province. From December 2024 to February 2025, we conducted a cross-sectional survey of caregivers of girls in selected classes at 12 schools, using multistage cluster convenience sampling. The questionnaire included Health Belief Model (HBM), Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), and Perceived Social Support Scale (PSSS) items. Factors were assessed with univariable and four-step hierarchical multiple linear regression, sequentially entering sociodemographic, HBM, TPB, and PSSS blocks. Willingness correlated with perceived susceptibility and severity, cues to action, attitudes, perceived behavioral control, and subjective norms. In univariable analyses, all HBM, TPB, and social-support dimensions except perceived barriers were positively associated with willingness. Hui caregivers had lower willingness, while higher education, middle income, and party/government-agency or public-institution employment predicted higher willingness. In hierarchical multiple regression, Hui ethnicity vs. Han ethnicity predicted lower willingness (B = -0.229, P = .003). Cues to action (β = 0.121, P = .024), perceived barriers (β = 0.128, P < .001), attitudes (β = 0.203, P < .001), perceived behavioral control (β = 0.107, P = .001), and subjective norms (β = 0.323, P < .001) were positively associated. HPV vaccination promotion should be tailored to Qinghai's ethnic autonomous prefectures, with authoritative school and primary-care recommendations, clear vaccine information, and vaccination-process support, while identifying barriers. Future qualitative and prospective implementation studies should clarify decision-making mechanisms and assess intervention acceptability and effects on vaccine uptake in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Association of platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and lymphocyte with HPV infection in adult women: a cross-sectional analysis
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection represents a major public health concern worldwide. Inflammatory indicators have been associated with various disease conditions. papers.title_zh: 成人女性血小板-淋巴细胞比值和淋巴细胞与人乳头瘤病毒感染的关系:一项横断面分析
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection represents a major public health concern worldwide. Inflammatory indicators have been associated with various disease conditions. However, the associations of platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), platelet (PLT), and lymphocyte (LYM) with HPV infection remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationships between PLR, PLT, LYM, and HPV infection. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2011 to 2016. PLR was calculated as PLT/LYM. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to evaluate the associations between PLR and HPV infection. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to calculate the area under the curve (AUC). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was applied to assess the association between LYM and HPV infection, and subgroup analyses with interaction tests were conducted. RESULTS: Among 5,415 adult females included in this study, 2,301 had HPV infection, and 3,114 did not. When PLR was analysed as a continuous variable, multivariable logistic regression showed a significant inverse association with HPV infection (odds ratio [OR] = 0.99). After categorising PLR into quartiles, participants in the highest PLR quartile (Q4: 143.70-477.14) showed lower odds of HPV infection compared with those in the lowest quartile (Q1: 12.86-92.60). The AUC values were 0.53, 0.64, and 0.72 for models I, II, and III, respectively. No significant association was observed between PLT and HPV infection. In contrast, LYM showed a significant positive association with HPV infection, with RCS analysis indicating a linear relationship. Interaction analysis suggested that this association varied according to PIR. CONCLUSION: Higher PLR was associated with lower odds of HPV infection, whereas higher LYM levels were associated with higher odds of HPV infection. These findings provide additional evidence regarding the associations between inflammatory indicators and HPV infection.

papers.title: FIGO/IGCS Statement on the efficacy of topical treatments for high-risk human papillomavirus in preventing CIN 3+ lesions
papers.abstract: Abstract Cervical cancer is caused by persistent high‐risk human papillomavirus (HR‐HPV) infection and remains a major global health burden despite available preventive strategies. Most HR‐HPV infections and associated low‐grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) regress spontaneously, yet increasing commercial promotion of topical therapies targeting HPV clearance has emerged in clinical practice. This FIGO/International Gynecologic Cancer Society (IGCS) Position Statement critically appraises the available evidence on topical treatments for HR‐HPV infection and LSIL, and provides evidence‐based recommendations for clinical practice and future research. No randomized controlled trial has been adequately designed or powered to evaluate the effect of topical therapies on the prevention of histologically confirmed high‐grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL/CIN3+). Available studies are characterized by small sample sizes, short follow‐up periods, heterogeneous populations, inadequate comparators, and reliance on surrogate endpoints of uncertain clinical relevance, including cytological regression, HPV nondetection, and immunohistochemical markers such as p16/Ki‐67. Published meta‐analyses reporting statistically significant improvements in virological and cytological surrogates are limited by substantial heterogeneity, publication bias, and follow‐up periods under 1 year. Product‐specific appraisal of Coriolus versicolor‐based and silicon dioxide/selenite‐based vaginal gels reveal additional methodological concerns, including retrospective trial registration, industry funding, and misinterpretation of findings consistent with the spin phenomenon. In the absence of high‐quality evidence demonstrating clinically meaningful benefit, FIGO and IGCS do not endorse the routine clinical use of any currently available topical agent for HR‐HPV infection or LSIL. Evidence‐based surveillance remains the standard of care. Future research should prioritize rigorous trial design with histologically confirmed HSIL/CIN3+ as the primary endpoint, adequate follow‐up of at least 3 years, and appropriate comparators. Clinical management should center on informed shared decision‐making and evidence‐based counseling, rather than on interventions lacking proven clinical benefit.

Most HR-HPV infections and associated low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) regress spontaneously, yet increasing commercial promotion of topical therapies targeting HPV clearance has emerged in clinical practice. This FIGO/International Gynecologic Cancer Society (IGCS) Position Statement critically appraises the available evidence on topical treatments for HR-HPV infection and LSIL, and provides evidence-based recommendations for clinical practice and future research. No randomized controlled trial has been adequately designed or powered to evaluate the effect of topical therapies on the prevention of histologically confirmed high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL/CIN3+). Available studies are characterized by small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, heterogeneous populations, inadequate comparators, and reliance on surrogate endpoints of uncertain clinical relevance, including cytological regression, HPV nondetection, and immunohistochemical markers such as p16/Ki-67. Published meta-analyses reporting statistically significant improvements in virological and cytological surrogates are limited by substantial heterogeneity, publication bias, and follow-up periods under 1 year. Product-specific appraisal of Coriolus versicolor-based and silicon dioxide/selenite-based vaginal gels reveal additional methodological concerns, including retrospective trial registration, industry funding, and misinterpretation of findings consistent with the spin phenomenon. In the absence of high-quality evidence demonstrating clinically meaningful benefit, FIGO and IGCS do not endorse the routine clinical use of any currently available topical agent for HR-HPV infection or LSIL. Evidence-based surveillance remains the standard of care. Future research should prioritize rigorous trial design with histologically confirmed HSIL/CIN3+ as the primary endpoint, adequate follow-up of at least 3 years, and appropriate comparators. Clinical management should center on informed shared decision-making and evidence-based counseling, rather than on interventions lacking proven clinical benefit.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the efficacy of topical treatments for high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection in preventing cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 3 (CIN 3+) lesions. The central question is whether these treatments can effectively prevent HR-HPV-related high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL/CIN3+).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review evaluates available studies on topical treatments for HR-HPV infection and low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL). These studies are characterized by small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, heterogeneous populations, inadequate comparators, and reliance on surrogate endpoints such as cytological regression, HPV nondetection, and immunohistochemical markers like p16/Ki-67. No randomized controlled trial has been adequately designed or powered to assess the effect of topical therapies on the prevention of histologically confirmed HSIL/CIN3+.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that there is no high-quality evidence demonstrating clinically meaningful benefit from topical treatments for HR-HPV infection or LSIL. The available meta-analyses are limited by substantial heterogeneity, publication bias, and follow-up periods under 1 year. Therefore, the FIGO/IGCS Position Statement does not endorse the routine clinical use of any currently available topical agent for HR-HPV infection or LSIL.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence is heterogeneous, with conflicting findings and methodological concerns such as small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, and reliance on surrogate endpoints. Additionally, product-specific studies on Coriolus versicolor-based and silicon dioxide/selenite-based vaginal gels raise issues like retrospective trial registration, industry funding, and misinterpretation of findings consistent with the spin phenomenon. There is a lack of studies with histologically confirmed HSIL/CIN3+ as the primary endpoint and adequate follow-up of at least 3 years.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize rigorous trial design with histologically confirmed HSIL/CIN3+ as the primary endpoint, adequate follow-up of at least 3 years, and appropriate comparators. Evidence-based surveillance remains the standard of care, and clinical management should focus on informed shared decision-making and evidence-based counseling rather than on interventions without proven clinical benefit.

analysis.summary_en: This review critically evaluates the evidence on the efficacy of topical treatments for high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection in preventing high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL/CIN3+). It highlights that no randomized controlled trial has been adequately designed or powered to assess this effect. Available studies are limited by small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, and reliance on surrogate endpoints. The review concludes that there is no high-quality evidence supporting the clinical benefit of these treatments, and thus, they are not endorsed for routine use. It emphasizes the need for future research with rigorous design, histologically confirmed endpoints, and longer follow-up periods. Clinical management should prioritize evidence-based surveillance and counseling over unproven interventions.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the efficacy of topical treatments for high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection in preventing cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 3 (CIN 3+) lesions. The central question is whether these treatments can effectively prevent HR-HPV-related high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL/CIN3+).
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review evaluates available studies on topical treatments for HR-HPV infection and low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL). These studies are characterized by small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, heterogeneous populations, inadequate comparators, and reliance on surrogate endpoints such as cytological regression, HPV nondetection, and immunohistochemical markers like p16/Ki-67. No randomized controlled trial has been adequately designed or powered to assess the effect of topical therapies on the prevention of histologically confirmed HSIL/CIN3+.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that there is no high-quality evidence demonstrating clinically meaningful benefit from topical treatments for HR-HPV infection or LSIL. The available meta-analyses are limited by substantial heterogeneity, publication bias, and follow-up periods under 1 year. Therefore, the FIGO/IGCS Position Statement does not endorse the routine clinical use of any currently available topical agent for HR-HPV infection or LSIL.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence is heterogeneous, with conflicting findings and methodological concerns such as small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, and reliance on surrogate endpoints. Additionally, product-specific studies on Coriolus versicolor-based and silicon dioxide/selenite-based vaginal gels raise issues like retrospective trial registration, industry funding, and misinterpretation of findings consistent with the spin phenomenon. There is a lack of studies with histologically confirmed HSIL/CIN3+ as the primary endpoint and adequate follow-up of at least 3 years.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize rigorous trial design with histologically confirmed HSIL/CIN3+ as the primary endpoint, adequate follow-up of at least 3 years, and appropriate comparators. Evidence-based surveillance remains the standard of care, and clinical management should focus on informed shared decision-making and evidence-based counseling rather than on interventions without proven clinical benefit.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述关注局部应用治疗对高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HR-HPV)感染预防宫颈上皮内瘤变3(CIN 3+)病变的效力。核心问题是这些治疗是否能有效预防与HR-HPV相关的高级别鳞状上皮内病变(HSIL/CIN3+).
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述评估了针对HR-HPV感染和低级别鳞状上皮内病变(LSIL)的局部应用治疗的研究。这些研究的特点包括样本量小、随访时间短、人群异质性高、对照不足以及依赖替代终点,如细胞学退行、HPV未检出以及免疫组化标志物如p16/Ki-67。目前尚无设计或样本量充足的研究能够评估局部治疗对预防组织学确诊的HSIL/CIN3+的效果。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出结论,目前没有高质量的证据表明局部应用治疗对HR-HPV感染或LSIL具有临床意义的益处。现有的荟萃分析受到显著异质性、发表偏倚以及随访时间不足1年的限制。因此,FIGO/IGCS立场声明不支持目前任何局部药物在HR-HPV感染或LSIL中的常规临床应用。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 证据具有异质性,存在相互矛盾的结果以及方法学上的问题,如样本量小、随访时间短和依赖替代终点。此外,基于Coriolus versicolor和二氧化硅/硒酸盐阴道凝胶的产品特定研究引发了诸如回顾性试验注册、行业资助以及与“spin phenomenon”一致的结果误读等问题。缺乏以组织学确诊的HSIL/CIN3+作为主要终点且随访时间至少为3年的研究。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应优先考虑严格的试验设计,以组织学证实的 HSIL/CIN3+ 作为主要终点,至少 3 年的充分随访,以及适当的比较。循证 监测 仍然是护理标准,临床管理应侧重于知情的共同决策和循证咨询,而不是没有经过证实的临床益处的干预措施。

papers.title_zh: FIGO/IGCS关于局部应用治疗对高危型人乳头瘤病毒感染预防宫颈上皮内瘤变3(CIN 3+)病变的效力声明
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Cervical cancer is caused by persistent high‐risk human papillomavirus (HR‐HPV) infection and remains a major global health burden despite available preventive strategies. Most HR‐HPV infections and associated low‐grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) regress spontaneously, yet increasing commercial promotion of topical therapies targeting HPV clearance has emerged in clinical practice. This FIGO/International Gynecologic Cancer Society (IGCS) Position Statement critically appraises the available evidence on topical treatments for HR‐HPV infection and LSIL, and provides evidence‐based recommendations for clinical practice and future research. No randomized controlled trial has been adequately designed or powered to evaluate the effect of topical therapies on the prevention of histologically confirmed high‐grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL/CIN3+). Available studies are characterized by small sample sizes, short follow‐up periods, heterogeneous populations, inadequate comparators, and reliance on surrogate endpoints of uncertain clinical relevance, including cytological regression, HPV nondetection, and immunohistochemical markers such as p16/Ki‐67. Published meta‐analyses reporting statistically significant improvements in virological and cytological surrogates are limited by substantial heterogeneity, publication bias, and follow‐up periods under 1 year. Product‐specific appraisal of Coriolus versicolor‐based and silicon dioxide/selenite‐based vaginal gels reveal additional methodological concerns, including retrospective trial registration, industry funding, and misinterpretation of findings consistent with the spin phenomenon. In the absence of high‐quality evidence demonstrating clinically meaningful benefit, FIGO and IGCS do not endorse the routine clinical use of any currently available topical agent for HR‐HPV infection or LSIL. Evidence‐based surveillance remains the standard of care. Future research should prioritize rigorous trial design with histologically confirmed HSIL/CIN3+ as the primary endpoint, adequate follow‐up of at least 3 years, and appropriate comparators. Clinical management should center on informed shared decision‐making and evidence‐based counseling, rather than on interventions lacking proven clinical benefit.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 宫颈癌 是由持续高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HR-HPV) 感染引起的,尽管有现有的预防策略,但它仍然是全球主要的健康负担。大多数 HR-HPV 感染和相关的低度鳞状上皮内病变 (LSIL) 会自发消退,但临床实践中已经出现了针对 HPV 清除的局部治疗的商业推广不断增加。该FIGO/国际妇科癌症协会 (IGCS) 立场声明严格评估了局部 治疗 针对 HR-HPV 感染和 LSIL 的现有证据,并为临床实践和未来研究提供了基于证据的建议。目前还没有充分设计或有效的随机对照试验来评估局部治疗对预防组织学证实的高级鳞状上皮内病变 (HSIL/CIN3+) 的效果。现有研究的特点是样本量小、随访期短、人群异质、比较器不足以及依赖临床相关性不确定的替代终点,包括细胞学回归、HPV未检出和免疫组织化学标记物,例如p16/Ki-67。已发表的荟萃分析报告了病毒学和细胞学替代指标在统计​​学上的显着改善,但受到显着异质性、发表偏倚和不到 1 年的随访期的限制。对云芝和二氧化硅/亚硒酸盐阴道凝胶的产品特定评估揭示了其他方法学问题,包括回顾性试验注册、行业资助以及对与旋转现象一致的研究结果的误解。在缺乏高质量证据证明具有临床意义的益处的情况下,FIGO 和 IGCS 不认可任何目前可用的局部用药治疗 HR-HPV 感染或 LSIL 的常规临床使用。循证 监测 仍然是护理标准。未来的研究应优先考虑严格的试验设计,以组织学证实的 HSIL/CIN3+ 作为主要终点,至少 3 年的充分随访,以及适当的比较。临床管理应以知情的共同决策和循证咨询为中心,而不是缺乏经过证实的临床益处的干预措施。

papers.title: Human papillomavirus (HPV) and HPV vaccine awareness in Indigenous communities in Northwest Territories, Canada
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted infection linked to several cancers, including cervical cancer, which ranks fourth in cancer incidence and mortality among women globally. Despite its significance, awareness of HPV and the HPV vaccine remains limited across many populations. This project assessed HPV and HPV vaccine awareness among Indigenous adults in Northwest Territories communities in Canada and explored factors influencing HPV vaccine utilization; such data have never been available or explored. METHODS: Using a community-based participatory research approach, quantitative and qualitative data were collected in 11 Indigenous communities in Northwest Territories. Indigenous adults aged 18 years and older were invited to complete a semi-structured questionnaire administered by trained local research assistants. Multiple logistic regression was used to examine potential associations among age, gender, education, and awareness of HPV and the HPV vaccine. A thematic analysis of qualitative data explored reasons for non-vaccination. RESULTS: Among the 221 participants (66.5% women; mean age 43.6 years (±13.9)), approximately half had heard of HPV, and fewer than one-third had heard of the HPV vaccine. Education emerged as a key factor, with individuals with lower educational attainment being significantly less aware of HPV (p < .000). Age (p < .033), gender (p < .019), and education (p < .004) predicted vaccine awareness, with women, individuals with higher education, and younger adults being more likely to have heard about the vaccine. Only 26.3% of participants aged up to 26 years had received the HPV vaccine. Qualitative data revealed that limited awareness and insufficient information about HPV and the vaccine are the main barriers to vaccination. Participants recommended enhancing vaccine promotion by raising awareness about the connection between HPV and cancer, as well as increasing educational efforts in schools and communities. CONCLUSIONS: Limited awareness of the HPV vaccine may contribute to low vaccination rates. Tailored and targeted interventions are crucial to increasing HPV vaccine utilization in Indigenous communities in Northwest Territories.

papers.title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)和HPV疫苗在加拿大西北地区原住民社区中的认知情况
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted infection linked to several cancers, including cervical cancer, which ranks fourth in cancer incidence and mortality among women globally. Despite its significance, awareness of HPV and the HPV vaccine remains limited across many populations. This project assessed HPV and HPV vaccine awareness among Indigenous adults in Northwest Territories communities in Canada and explored factors influencing HPV vaccine utilization; such data have never been available or explored. METHODS: Using a community-based participatory research approach, quantitative and qualitative data were collected in 11 Indigenous communities in Northwest Territories. Indigenous adults aged 18 years and older were invited to complete a semi-structured questionnaire administered by trained local research assistants. Multiple logistic regression was used to examine potential associations among age, gender, education, and awareness of HPV and the HPV vaccine. A thematic analysis of qualitative data explored reasons for non-vaccination. RESULTS: Among the 221 participants (66.5% women; mean age 43.6 years (±13.9)), approximately half had heard of HPV, and fewer than one-third had heard of the HPV vaccine. Education emerged as a key factor, with individuals with lower educational attainment being significantly less aware of HPV (p < .000). Age (p < .033), gender (p < .019), and education (p < .004) predicted vaccine awareness, with women, individuals with higher education, and younger adults being more likely to have heard about the vaccine. Only 26.3% of participants aged up to 26 years had received the HPV vaccine. Qualitative data revealed that limited awareness and insufficient information about HPV and the vaccine are the main barriers to vaccination. Participants recommended enhancing vaccine promotion by raising awareness about the connection between HPV and cancer, as well as increasing educational efforts in schools and communities. CONCLUSIONS: Limited awareness of the HPV vaccine may contribute to low vaccination rates. Tailored and targeted interventions are crucial to increasing HPV vaccine utilization in Indigenous communities in Northwest Territories.
papers.abstract_zh: 目的:人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)是一种常见的性传播感染,与多种癌症有关,包括宫颈癌,其在全球女性中癌症发病率和死亡率排名第四。尽管其重要性显著,但许多人群中对HPV及其疫苗的认知仍然有限。本研究评估了加拿大西北地区原住民社区中成年原住民对HPV及其疫苗的认知情况,并探讨了影响HPV疫苗使用因素;此类数据此前从未被收集或研究过。方法:采用基于社区的参与式研究方法,在西北地区的11个原住民社区中收集定量和定性数据。邀请18岁及以上的原住民成年人完成由受过培训的当地研究人员进行的半结构化问卷。使用多因素Logistic回归分析年龄、性别、教育水平与HPV及其疫苗认知之间的潜在关联。对定性数据进行主题分析,探讨未接种HPV疫苗的原因。结果:在221名参与者中(女性占66.5%;平均年龄43.6岁(±13.9)),约有一半听说过HPV,而不到三分之一听说过HPV疫苗。教育水平是一个关键因素,教育程度较低的个体对HPV的认知显著较低(p < .000)。年龄(p < .033)、性别(p < .019)和教育水平(p < .004)预测了HPV疫苗的认知,女性、受教育程度较高者和年轻成年人更有可能听说过HPV疫苗。仅26.3%的年龄在26岁及以下的参与者接种过HPV疫苗。定性数据表明,对HPV及其疫苗的认知不足和相关信息的缺乏是影响疫苗接种的主要障碍。参与者建议通过提高对HPV与癌症之间联系的认识以及在学校和社区中加强教育来增强HPV疫苗的推广。结论:HPV疫苗认知的不足可能与疫苗接种率低有关。在加拿大西北地区的原住民社区中,需要有针对性的干预措施来提高HPV疫苗的使用率。

papers.title: Predominance of non-16/18 high-risk human papilloma-virus (HPV) genotypes among female sex workers in Papua, Indonesia: Implications for vaccine coverage
papers.abstract: Background Female sex workers face high occupational exposure to human papillomavirus (HPV), but to our knowledge no molecular HPV genotyping data have been published for Papua, Indonesia, where cervical screening reaches few women. Non-16/18 genotypes account for a large share of HPV infection across Asia, relevant to vaccine policy. We aimed to measure high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) prevalence, describe the genotypes present, and identify factors associated with HR-HPV positivity among FSWs in Jayapura. Methods In this cross-sectional study, female sex workers attending a reproductive health centre in Jayapura, Papua, were recruited by consecutive sampling in August 2025. Cervical specimens were genotyped for HR-HPV with a real-time PCR assay distinguishing HPV16, HPV18 and a pooled channel covering 12 high-risk types. A structured questionnaire recorded age, duration of sex work, condom use, vaccination status, sexually transmitted infection history and sexual contact frequency. Candidate predictors were screened bivariately before multivariable logistic regression. Results Of 75 participants, 33 (44%; 95% CI 33–56) were HR-HPV positive. Of these, 30 (91%; 95% CI 76–98) carried at least one non-16/18 genotype, and only three were attributable to HPV16 or HPV18 alone. Three women (4%) reported prior HPV vaccination. After adjustment for sexual contact frequency, each additional year of age was associated with lower odds of HR-HPV positivity (adjusted odds ratio 0.928, 95% CI 0.871–0.990, p = 0.023). The association with sexual contact frequency was positive but not significant (1.322, 95% CI 0.986–1.773, p = 0.062). Condom use was associated bivariately but excluded from the final model owing to unstable estimates. Conclusions HR-HPV infection is common among female sex workers in Papua and mostly involves non HPV16 and HPV18 genotypes, which the current quadrivalent national programme does not cover. These data support nonavalent vaccination and HPV-DNA screening for female sex workers, and make expanded screening in the general population a priority for provincial health authorities in Papua.

We aimed to measure high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) prevalence, describe the genotypes present, and identify factors associated with HR-HPV positivity among FSWs in Jayapura. Methods In this cross-sectional study, female sex workers attending a reproductive health centre in Jayapura, Papua, were recruited by consecutive sampling in August 2025. Cervical specimens were genotyped for HR-HPV with a real-time PCR assay distinguishing HPV16, HPV18 and a pooled channel covering 12 high-risk types. A structured questionnaire recorded age, duration of sex work, condom use, vaccination status, sexually transmitted infection history and sexual contact frequency. Candidate predictors were screened bivariately before multivariable logistic regression. Results Of 75 participants, 33 (44%; 95% CI 33–56) were HR-HPV positive. Of these, 30 (91%; 95% CI 76–98) carried at least one non-16/18 genotype, and only three were attributable to HPV16 or HPV18 alone. Three women (4%) reported prior HPV vaccination. After adjustment for sexual contact frequency, each additional year of age was associated with lower odds of HR-HPV positivity (adjusted odds ratio 0.928, 95% CI 0.871–0.990, p = 0.023). The association with sexual contact frequency was positive but not significant (1.322, 95% CI 0.986–1.773, p = 0.062). Condom use was associated bivariately but excluded from the final model owing to unstable estimates. Conclusions HR-HPV infection is common among female sex workers in Papua and mostly involves non HPV16 and HPV18 genotypes, which the current quadrivalent national programme does not cover. These data support nonavalent vaccination and HPV-DNA screening for female sex workers, and make expanded screening in the general population a priority for provincial health authorities in Papua.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这项横断面研究中,于 2025 年 8 月通过连续抽样招募了在巴布亚查亚普拉生殖健康中心就诊的女性性工作者。在 75 名参与者中,33 人(44%;95% CI 33-56)HR-HPV 呈阳性。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过实时 PCR 检测对宫颈标本进行 HR-HPV 基因分型,区分 HPV16、HPV18 和涵盖 12 种高危类型的汇集通道。结构化调查问卷记录了年龄、性工作持续时间、安全套使用情况、疫苗接种 状况、性传播感染史和性接触频率。在多变量逻辑回归之前对候选预测因子进行双变量筛选。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些数据支持对女性性工作者进行非病毒 疫苗接种 和 HPV-DNA 筛查,并使在普通人群中扩大筛查成为巴布亚省卫生当局的优先事项。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究结果的普遍性或除年龄和性接触频率之外的混杂因素的可能性。

papers.title: Immunogenicity and Safety of the 9-valent Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccine Administered as 2-Dose or 3-Dose Regimens in Japanese Boys and Girls Aged 9-15 Years
papers.abstract: A phase III open-label study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the 9-valent human papillomavirus (9vHPV) vaccine in Japanese boys and girls. Japanese boys aged 9-15 years (n = 105) received a 3-dose (Day 1, Month 2, and Month 6) regimen; Japanese boys (n = 104) and girls aged 9-14 years (n = 105) received a 2-dose (Day 1 and Month 6) regimen. Antibody responses to HPV6/11/16/18/31/33/45/52/58 were assessed at Month 7, 18, and 30 using a competitive Luminex immunoassay. Injection-site adverse events (AEs; Days 1 to 5 post-dose), systemic AEs (Days 1 to 15 post-dose), and serious AEs (duration of study) were assessed. At Month 7, for HPV types targeted by the 9vHPV vaccine, seroconversion rates were 100% in all three arms, and in cross-study comparisons with efficacy studies, anti-HPV geometric mean titers in boys were noninferior to those in Japanese men aged 16-26 years, and in girls were noninferior to those in Japanese women aged 16-26 years. Most injection-site AEs were mild to moderate in intensity. No deaths or vaccine-related serious AEs were observed. These results support immunobridging of efficacy findings in Japanese men and women to Japanese boys and girls. The 9vHPV vaccine was generally well tolerated.

papers.title: Human papillomavirus infection and risk of cardiovascular disease: A population-based matched cohort study with sibling analysis
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of human papillomavirus (HPV) in cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains unclear. We aimed to investigate the associations of HPV infection with incident CVD and CVD-related mortality. METHODS AND FINDINGS: In this population-based matched cohort study based on Swedish national registers, we identified women with an incident HPV infection during 2006 and 2024 (N = 497,445), and age-matched each woman with five women without infection. The time-varying associations between HPV infection and CVD were assessed using flexible parametric models, which also provided hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) after adjusting for sociodemographic factors, HPV vaccination, chronic diseases, and parental history of related diseases. To control for familial factors, we also compared 143,787 women with HPV infection to their 174,637 unaffected full siblings. A total of 28,793 and 128,373 incident CVDs were identified in women with and without HPV infection (Incidence: 8.27 and 7.93 per 1,000 person-years), respectively. Additionally, 1,221 and 4,941 CVD-related deaths were observed among women with and without HPV infection (Mortality: 33.73 and 29.39 per 100,000 person-years), respectively. The risks of incident CVD and mortality were most pronounced within the first follow-up year and attenuated thereafter. Overall, women with HPV infection had an increased risk of incident CVD (adjusted HR 1.07, 95% CI [1.05, 1.08], absolute rate difference 0.53 per 1,000 person-years, population-attributable fraction 1.16%) and CVD-related mortality (adjusted HR 1.25, 95% CI [1.16, 1.34], absolute rate difference 6.71 per 100,000 person-years, population-attributable fraction 4.12%) than those without. During the first follow-up year, the adjusted HRs for incident CVD and CVD-related mortality were 1.43 (95% CI [1.38, 1.48]) and 1.86 (95% CI [1.41, 2.45]), respectively. Beyond the first follow-up year, the corresponding adjusted HRs decreased to 1.02 (95% CI [1.01, 1.04]) for incident CVD and 1.21 (95% CI [1.12, 1.30]) for CVD-related mortality. In sibling comparisons, positive associations with both outcomes were also observed. Women with HPV infection had fully adjusted HRs of 1.05 (95% CI [1.01, 1.08]) for incident CVD and 1.25 (95% CI [1.01, 1.53]) for CVD-related mortality compared to their siblings without HPV infections. The main limitations of this study are its observational design, which precludes causal inference between HPV infection and CVD, and the potential misclassification of HPV infection, which may have biased the association towards the null. CONCLUSIONS: HPV infection was associated with increased risk of incident CVD and CVD-related mortality. The findings suggested that clinicians should be aware of a slightly elevated CVD risk in women with HPV, especially during the first year following an infection. However, given the small absolute difference, women should not be unduly concerned.

papers.title: A droplet digital PCR assay targeting 16 human papillomavirus genotypes
papers.abstract: Cervical screening with high-precision assays such as human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA testing is essential for the detection and treatment of precancerous lesions. HPV genotypes have different oncogenic potential and require different clinical management, illustrating the importance of extended genotyping. HPV quantification has demonstrated clinical relevance in both diagnosis and treatment. To develop a droplet digital PCR assay for the detection and quantification of 16 HPV genotypes, with comparison to a commercial test and validation on clinical samples. Primers and probes were designed to target the E6 region of 16 HPV genotypes: 16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, 68, 73 and 82. Each target was evaluated to assess performance and reliability using synthetic DNA constructs, quantified international reference standards and clinical screening samples ( n =303) genotyped using the Seegene Anyplex II HR HPV Detection assay. Each assay demonstrated high target specificity, without cross-reactivity observed among the HPV genotypes selected. Using international molecular standards, the assay reliably detected high-risk genotypes across serial dilutions, with detection down to the level of one international unit or genome equivalent per microlitre. When applied to clinical samples with and without a histological diagnosis of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2 or worse (CIN2+), the assay reliably detected key HPV genotypes, with the exception of 7 of 234 (3%) of HPV-positive samples, all of which exhibited very low viral load. Although previous studies have described digital PCR methods targeting HPV E6, they have typically focused on a limited number of genotypes. This study expands upon existing methodology by introducing a sensitive and specific method for detection and quantification of 16 high-risk and potentially high-risk HPV genotypes.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 开发一种液滴数字 PCR 检测方法,用于检测和定量 16 种 HPV 基因型,并与临床样本的商业测试和验证进行比较。使用合成 DNA 构建体、量化的国际参考标准和使用 Seegene Anyplex II HR HPV 检测分析进行基因分型的临床筛查样本 (n = 303) 来评估每个靶点的性能和可靠性。
elements_zh.methods: 引物和探针设计用于靶向 16 种 HPV 基因型的 E6 区域:16、18、31、33、35、39、45、51、52、56、58、59、66、68、73 和 82。每种检测均显示出高靶点特异性,在所选 HPV 基因型之间未观察到交叉反应。使用国际分子标准,该检测方法能够可靠地检测连续稀释的高风险基因型,检测水平可低至每微升一个国际单位或 基因组 当量的水平。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: HPV定量在诊断和治疗中均显示出临床相关性。本研究通过引入一种敏感且特异的方法,扩展了现有技术,用于检测和定量16种高危型及潜在高危型HPV基因型。

HPV genotypes have different oncogenic potential and require different clinical management, illustrating the importance of extended genotyping. HPV quantification has demonstrated clinical relevance in both diagnosis and treatment. To develop a droplet digital PCR assay for the detection and quantification of 16 HPV genotypes, with comparison to a commercial test and validation on clinical samples. Primers and probes were designed to target the E6 region of 16 HPV genotypes: 16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, 68, 73 and 82. Each target was evaluated to assess performance and reliability using synthetic DNA constructs, quantified international reference standards and clinical screening samples ( n =303) genotyped using the Seegene Anyplex II HR HPV Detection assay. Each assay demonstrated high target specificity, without cross-reactivity observed among the HPV genotypes selected. Using international molecular standards, the assay reliably detected high-risk genotypes across serial dilutions, with detection down to the level of one international unit or genome equivalent per microlitre. When applied to clinical samples with and without a histological diagnosis of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2 or worse (CIN2+), the assay reliably detected key HPV genotypes, with the exception of 7 of 234 (3%) of HPV-positive samples, all of which exhibited very low viral load. Although previous studies have described digital PCR methods targeting HPV E6, they have typically focused on a limited number of genotypes. This study expands upon existing methodology by introducing a sensitive and specific method for detection and quantification of 16 high-risk and potentially high-risk HPV genotypes.

papers.title: Clinical Utility of Human Papillomavirus ctDNA for Treatment Monitoring and Recurrence Prediction in Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Abstract Locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC), defined as FIGO 2018 stages IB3-IVA, is associated with relapse rates between 30 and 60% after definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT). The current strategy for monitoring is based on physical examinations and imaging, which could be confounded by radiation-induced fibrosis, and existing biomarkers like squamous cell carcinoma antigen lack sensitivity in detecting minimal residual disease (MRD). Circulating tumor DNA derived from human papillomavirus (HPV ctDNA) has recently been shown to be useful for molecular surveillance through liquid biopsies. This article aims to investigate the clinical significance of HPV ctDNA in monitoring the response to therapy and predicting recurrence in patients with LACC. This study is a systematic review of Scopus and PubMed databases (2017–2026) of articles examining the longitudinal detection of HPV ctDNA as a molecular marker in patients with LACC undergoing definitive CRT. Studies utilizing sensitive molecular techniques such as droplet digital polymerase chain reaction and next-generation sequencing were included and analyzed outcomes including MRD, recurrence, and survival. A total of seven papers were selected, utilizing results from large-scale cohort studies, such as CALLA Phase III trial and BioRAIDs trial conducted in Europe. The detection rate of HPV ctDNA at the time of diagnosis was 60.8 to 98.9%, correlating with tumor burden, defined by FIGO staging and nodal disease. The persistence of ctDNA at the end of treatment or 3 months following CRT as evidence of MRD consistently indicated a worse prognosis in terms of relapse. ctDNA positivity predicted worse progression-free survival (hazard ratio: 2.53–14.25) and predated radiographic relapse by 5.5 to 10 months. HPV ctDNA may serve as a promising adjunctive biomarker for MRD detection and early relapse prediction in LACC.
papers.journal: Indian Journal of Medical and Paediatric Oncology

papers.title_original: Clinical Utility of Human Papillomavirus ctDNA for Treatment Monitoring and Recurrence Prediction in Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer: A Systematic Review

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the clinical utility of human papillomavirus (HPV) circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for treatment monitoring and recurrence prediction in patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC). The central question is whether HPV ctDNA can serve as a reliable biomarker for detecting minimal residual disease (MRD) and predicting relapse following definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of studies retrieved from Scopus and PubMed databases between 2017 and 2026. It includes seven papers that examine the longitudinal detection of HPV ctDNA as a molecular marker in patients with LACC undergoing CRT. The studies analyzed outcomes such as MRD, recurrence, and survival, utilizing sensitive molecular techniques like droplet digital polymerase chain reaction and next-generation sequencing.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HPV ctDNA positivity was associated with worse progression-free survival, with hazard ratios ranging from 2.53 to 14.25. It also predicted radiographic relapse up to 10 months earlier. The persistence of HPV ctDNA at the end of treatment or 3 months post-CRT was consistently linked to a higher risk of relapse, indicating its potential as a biomarker for MRD detection and early recurrence prediction.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The current strategy for monitoring LACC relies on physical exams and imaging, which may be confounded by radiation-induced fibrosis. Existing biomarkers like squamous cell carcinoma antigen lack sensitivity in detecting MRD. The review highlights the need for further research to validate the clinical utility of HPV ctDNA in diverse populations and to address methodological limitations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: There is a clear need for additional studies to evaluate the effectiveness of HPV ctDNA in different patient populations and to refine its use in clinical practice. Research should also focus on improving sensitivity and specificity, as well as integrating HPV ctDNA testing into routine monitoring protocols for LACC patients.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the clinical utility of human papillomavirus (HPV) circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for monitoring treatment response and predicting recurrence in patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC). The review highlights that HPV ctDNA positivity correlates with worse progression-free survival and can detect minimal residual disease (MRD) earlier than conventional methods. While the evidence supports its potential as a biomarker, limitations in sensitivity and the need for further validation in diverse populations remain. The findings suggest that HPV ctDNA could serve as an adjunctive tool for MRD detection and recurrence prediction, but more research is required to establish its role in clinical practice.

papers.title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒循环肿瘤DNA在局部晚期宫颈癌患者治疗监测和复发预测中的临床应用:系统综述
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC), defined as FIGO 2018 stages IB3-IVA, is associated with relapse rates between 30 and 60% after definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT). The current strategy for monitoring is based on physical examinations and imaging, which could be confounded by radiation-induced fibrosis, and existing biomarkers like squamous cell carcinoma antigen lack sensitivity in detecting minimal residual disease (MRD). Circulating tumor DNA derived from human papillomavirus (HPV ctDNA) has recently been shown to be useful for molecular surveillance through liquid biopsies. This article aims to investigate the clinical significance of HPV ctDNA in monitoring the response to therapy and predicting recurrence in patients with LACC. This study is a systematic review of Scopus and PubMed databases (2017–2026) of articles examining the longitudinal detection of HPV ctDNA as a molecular marker in patients with LACC undergoing definitive CRT. Studies utilizing sensitive molecular techniques such as droplet digital polymerase chain reaction and next-generation sequencing were included and analyzed outcomes including MRD, recurrence, and survival. A total of seven papers were selected, utilizing results from large-scale cohort studies, such as CALLA Phase III trial and BioRAIDs trial conducted in Europe. The detection rate of HPV ctDNA at the time of diagnosis was 60.8 to 98.9%, correlating with tumor burden, defined by FIGO staging and nodal disease. The persistence of ctDNA at the end of treatment or 3 months following CRT as evidence of MRD consistently indicated a worse prognosis in terms of relapse. ctDNA positivity predicted worse progression-free survival (hazard ratio: 2.53–14.25) and predated radiographic relapse by 5.5 to 10 months. HPV ctDNA may serve as a promising adjunctive biomarker for MRD detection and early relapse prediction in LACC.

papers.title: Projections of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination impact on non-cervical cancer outcomes among women in 117 low- and middle-income countries: a modelling study.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a leading cause of both cervical and non-cervical cancers, including anal, oropharyngeal, vaginal and vulvar cancers. While most HPV vaccination impact assessments have focused on preventing cervical cancer among women, the broader benefits of vaccination against other HPV-attributable cancers in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remain less explored. METHODS: We used a static cohort model to assess the potential health impact of bivalent HPV vaccination on HPV-attributable female non-cervical cancers in 117 LMICs from 2030 to 2100. The model incorporated country-specific data on cancer mortality, HPV type distribution, demographic projections and vaccine coverage. Sensitivity analyses were performed to account for uncertainties in cancer incidence, cancer mortality and HPV type distribution. RESULTS: Our projections suggest that HPV vaccination could contribute to prevention of approximately five 90 000 cases of anal, 880 000 cases of oropharyngeal, 1.27 million cases of vaginal and 2.18 million cases of vulvar cancers over the analytic period. In total, 3.02 million deaths from these non-cervical cancers among women could be averted by 2100. The African region is expected to see the largest relative reductions in both cases and deaths while the European region showed the smallest gains. By the end of the century, 58 countries are projected to reach at least a 25% reduction in anal cancer mortality compared with just 25 countries for oropharyngeal cancer. These findings reflect substantial regional disparities in both burden and vaccination impact. CONCLUSION: HPV vaccination holds considerable promise in reducing the burden of non-cervical cancers among women in LMICs, especially in regions with high incidence and limited access to care. Recognising and harnessing these broader benefits can strengthen the public health case for scaling up vaccine access, implementing region-specific strategies and investing in equitable healthcare systems to decrease global disparities.

papers.title_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 对 117 个低收入和中等收入国家女性非 宫颈癌 结果的影响的预测:一项建模研究。
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a leading cause of both cervical and non-cervical cancers, including anal, oropharyngeal, vaginal and vulvar cancers. While most HPV vaccination impact assessments have focused on preventing cervical cancer among women, the broader benefits of vaccination against other HPV-attributable cancers in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remain less explored. METHODS: We used a static cohort model to assess the potential health impact of bivalent HPV vaccination on HPV-attributable female non-cervical cancers in 117 LMICs from 2030 to 2100. The model incorporated country-specific data on cancer mortality, HPV type distribution, demographic projections and vaccine coverage. Sensitivity analyses were performed to account for uncertainties in cancer incidence, cancer mortality and HPV type distribution. RESULTS: Our projections suggest that HPV vaccination could contribute to prevention of approximately five 90 000 cases of anal, 880 000 cases of oropharyngeal, 1.27 million cases of vaginal and 2.18 million cases of vulvar cancers over the analytic period. In total, 3.02 million deaths from these non-cervical cancers among women could be averted by 2100. The African region is expected to see the largest relative reductions in both cases and deaths while the European region showed the smallest gains. By the end of the century, 58 countries are projected to reach at least a 25% reduction in anal cancer mortality compared with just 25 countries for oropharyngeal cancer. These findings reflect substantial regional disparities in both burden and vaccination impact. CONCLUSION: HPV vaccination holds considerable promise in reducing the burden of non-cervical cancers among women in LMICs, especially in regions with high incidence and limited access to care. Recognising and harnessing these broader benefits can strengthen the public health case for scaling up vaccine access, implementing region-specific strategies and investing in equitable healthcare systems to decrease global disparities.

papers.title: A multidisciplinary approach to education: The design and production of a novel eLearning resource on the link between human papillomavirus and head and neck cancer
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: An understanding of the role of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) in head and neck cancer (HNC) has developed rapidly over the last decade, with a shift in epidemiology in the patient population and global increase in disease. DISCUSSION: Following a previous evaluation of healthcare professionals' knowledge and confidence regarding HPV and its association with HNC, a clear gap in understanding was identified. In response to that information, we have developed this novel eLearning package focused on HPV-positive HNC, designed to address educational needs and support improved clinical practice. E-Learning has been widely recognised as an accessible, flexible, and cost-effective approach to continuous professional development (CPD) within healthcare settings. In the context of a rapidly evolving area of oncology and given the emphasis on role diversification within the UK's NHS Workforce Plan, it was considered highly relevant to leverage this method of education. The goal was not only to inform healthcare professionals about the connection between HPV and HNC but also to use this platform to visually illustrate the multidisciplinary team's (MDT's) involvement in patient care and highlight the roles of various professionals working collaboratively in today's modern, interprofessional environment. CONCLUSION: Here we have reported the main aims, designs and initial production of the eLearning resource, detailing the approach and design principles, especially in terms of interactivity, flexibility and accessibility; highlighting the importance of key voices, especially that of the patient, and summarising the main challenges involved. Since launch, 134 healthcare professionals have engaged with the resource just in the local hospital Trust; a much wider diversity of disciplines than initially imagined. The package has been recommended by Clinical Oncologists as a fundamental resource for training information on HPV, since the content and learning outcomes for staff are interchangeable across the multiple cancer sites that the virus is attributable to. With the widespread uptake, there is a need for further evaluation and development, with possible extension to a national audience and other HPV related cancer types. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: The human papillomavirus (HPV) is linked to a growing number of head and neck cancers, creating a need for healthcare professionals to stay up to date with current knowledge. This project developed an interactive online learning resource to improve understanding of HPV-related head and neck cancer and to demonstrate how different healthcare professionals work together to care for patients. This study found strong early engagement with the resource from a wide range of healthcare professionals, and it has been recommended as a valuable training tool. This matters because accessible education may help improve knowledge, support collaborative care, and strengthen training in cancers linked to HPV.

papers.title: Preliminary Development and Assessment of a Multiplex Assay for Human Papillomavirus Antibody Detection Using Commercial L1 Proteins
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cancers are preventable with vaccination. Serologic assays monitor antibody responses, but their complexity and cost pose limitations when evaluating population level immunity. We developed an L1-based assay for the detection of multiple type-specific HPV antibodies. METHODS: The Luminex-based assay used recombinant L1 proteins from seven HPVs (HPV-6/11/16/18/35/45/58) for the detection of type-specific immunoglobulin (Ig)G and IgA. Cutoffs were established using plasma from infants and children. The assay was optimized and qualified using a sample set from a blinded proficiency panel developed at the Frederick National Laboratory for Cancer Research. RESULTS: Sensitivity and specificity for anti-HPV-6/11/16/18/58 IgG were 100% at the Mean + 3 standard deviation [SD] and Mean + 5 SD thresholds. Sensitivity for HPV-45 was 100% and 92.9% at the +3 SD and +5 SD thresholds, respectively. IgA detection showed moderate positivity among vaccinated individuals, with peak estimates of 96.4% (HPV-11) and 85.7% (HPV-58) at the +3 SD threshold. IgA was correlated with IgG (Spearman's ρ = 0.74). The L1-assay differentiated high, intermediate, low, and negative response groups from the blinded samples for all HPV genotypes (p < 0.0001). CONCLUSION: The L1-binding assay has the potential to be a scalable option for high-throughput detection of broad-spectrum HPV immunoglobulins, but further standardization and validation are needed.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop and assess a multiplex assay for detecting type-specific HPV antibodies using commercial L1 proteins. The L1-based assay was designed to detect IgG and IgA antibodies against seven HPV types (6, 11, 16, 18, 35, 45, and 58). The assay was optimized and validated using a blinded proficiency panel. Results showed high sensitivity and specificity for IgG antibodies against HPV-6, 11, 16, 18, and 58, with moderate sensitivity for HPV-45. IgA detection was also observed, showing moderate positivity among vaccinated individuals and a correlation with IgG. The authors concluded that the assay has potential for scalable, high-throughput detection of HPV immunoglobulins but emphasized the need for further standardization and validation. The study provides a foundation for improving serologic monitoring of HPV immunity, which could support public health efforts in vaccination programs.

papers.title: Gelatin–PVA Hydrogel Composite-Based Immunosensing Interface for Early Detection of HPV16-Driven Cervical Cancer
papers.abstract: Abstract Viral oncoprotein HPV16 E6 is a critical mediator of cervical malignancy and a promising biomarker for early-stage detection of cervical cancer. Current diagnostic approaches centered around morphology-based screening and DNA-based assays emphasize the need for noninvasive, affordable, and highly sensitive urine-based detection methods targeting HPV16 E6 oncoprotein for early diagnosis. This study introduces a noninvasive diagnostic strategy using a gelatin–PVA (G-PVA) hydrogel composite-based electrochemical biosensor for HPV16 E6 oncoprotein detection in spiked urine samples. The proposed platform integrates chemically crosslinked G-PVA hydrogel as a transducing matrix for biosensing offering superior biocompatibility, electrochemical stability, and enhanced surface area for antibody immobilization. The biosensor platform demonstrates robust electrochemical performance with a broad dynamic range (1 pg mL–1 to 1 μg mL–1), ultra-low detection limit (0.56 pg mL–1), and quantification limit (1.88 pg mL–1). Furthermore, it exhibits a sensitivity of 37 μA cm–2 log–1 (pg mL–1) along with good reproducibility and specificity toward E6 oncoprotein even in complex media such as artificial urine. Overall, this study demonstrates the feasibility of the G-PVA hydrogel composite-based biosensor as an affordable, noninvasive, point-of-care (POC) detection platform representing significant advancement toward early detection of HPV16-associated cervical cancer.

papers.title_zh: 基于明胶-聚乙烯醇水凝胶复合材料的免疫传感界面用于HPV16驱动的宫颈癌的早期检测
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Viral oncoprotein HPV16 E6 is a critical mediator of cervical malignancy and a promising biomarker for early-stage detection of cervical cancer. Current diagnostic approaches centered around morphology-based screening and DNA-based assays emphasize the need for noninvasive, affordable, and highly sensitive urine-based detection methods targeting HPV16 E6 oncoprotein for early diagnosis. This study introduces a noninvasive diagnostic strategy using a gelatin–PVA (G-PVA) hydrogel composite-based electrochemical biosensor for HPV16 E6 oncoprotein detection in spiked urine samples. The proposed platform integrates chemically crosslinked G-PVA hydrogel as a transducing matrix for biosensing offering superior biocompatibility, electrochemical stability, and enhanced surface area for antibody immobilization. The biosensor platform demonstrates robust electrochemical performance with a broad dynamic range (1 pg mL–1 to 1 μg mL–1), ultra-low detection limit (0.56 pg mL–1), and quantification limit (1.88 pg mL–1). Furthermore, it exhibits a sensitivity of 37 μA cm–2 log–1 (pg mL–1) along with good reproducibility and specificity toward E6 oncoprotein even in complex media such as artificial urine. Overall, this study demonstrates the feasibility of the G-PVA hydrogel composite-based biosensor as an affordable, noninvasive, point-of-care (POC) detection platform representing significant advancement toward early detection of HPV16-associated cervical cancer.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)16的癌基因蛋白E6是宫颈恶性肿瘤的关键介导因子,也是早期检测宫颈癌的有前景的生物标志物。目前以形态学筛查和DNA检测为基础的诊断方法强调需要针对HPV16 E6癌基因蛋白的非侵入性、经济实惠且高度敏感的尿液检测方法,以实现早期诊断的检测。本研究引入了一种基于明胶-聚乙烯醇(G-PVA)水凝胶复合材料的电化学生物传感器,用于检测人工尿液样本中HPV16 E6癌基因蛋白。该平台采用化学交联的G-PVA水凝胶作为生物传感的转导基质,具有优异的生物相容性、电化学稳定性以及增强的抗体固定表面积。生物传感器平台表现出稳健的电化学性能,具有广泛的动态范围(1 pg mL–1至1 μg mL–1)、超低检测限(0.56 pg mL–1)和定量限(1.88 pg mL–1)。此外,即使在复杂介质如人工尿液中,该生物传感器也表现出对E6癌基因蛋白的良好灵敏度(37 μA cm–2 log–1 [pg mL–1])以及良好的可重复性和特异性。总体而言,本研究展示了基于G-PVA水凝胶复合材料的生物传感器作为经济实惠、非侵入性、即时检测(POC)平台在HPV16相关宫颈癌早期检测中的可行性,代表了该领域的重要进展。

papers.title: Human Papillomavirus-Related Diseases in Urology: Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention, and Clinical Considerations for Healthcare Providers
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) has long been regarded as a gynecologic pathogen, yet its disease burden in men is substantial and rapidly increasing. In Korea, the prevalence of anogenital warts in men has tripled over the past decade, penile cancer continues to rise, and HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) incidence in men has already exceeded that of cervical cancer in comparable high-income countries. This review reframes HPV as an urgent urological, occupational, and public health concern. Drawing primarily on the 2023 Korean Sexually Transmitted Infection (STI) Guidelines and the 2021 U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention STI Treatment Guidelines, supplemented by original primary literature retrieved from PubMed, we address: (1) the male-specific epidemiological shift; (2) nonsexual and occupational transmission routes, with particular emphasis on surgical smoke; (3) evidence-based infection control in urology practice; (4) clinical management of anogenital warts; (5) male HPV vaccination policy, international comparisons, and cost-effectiveness; and (6) future research priorities including OPC prevention, HPV and male infertility, and the need for urology-specific infection control guidelines. From 2026, Korea will include 12-year-old boys in its National Immunization Program—the first gender-neutral HPV vaccination policy in Korea. This review highlights the expanding and indispensable role of urologists in HPV management and emphasizes that infection control vigilance and gender-neutral vaccination strategies are essential to reduce the mounting societal burden of HPV-related diseases. This review provides a practical framework for urologists to integrate HPV prevention, infection control, and vaccination counseling into routine clinical practice.

papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 长期以来被认为是一种妇科病原体,但其在男性中的疾病负担却很大且迅速增加。在韩国,过去十年中男性肛门生殖器疣的 发病率 增加了两倍,阴茎癌持续上升,男性 HPV 阳性口咽癌 (OPC) 发病率 已经超过了可比高收入国家的 发病率。这篇综述将 HPV 重新定义为一个紧迫的泌尿科、职业和公共卫生问题。主要借鉴 2023 年韩国性传播感染 (STI) 指南和 2021 年美国疾病控制与预防中心 STI 治疗 指南,并辅以从 PubMed 检索到的原始原始文献,我们解决了:(1) 男性特异性流行病学转变;(2)非性和职业性的传播途径,特别强调手术烟雾;(3)泌尿外科实践中循证感染控制;(4)肛门生殖器疣的临床治疗;(5)男性HPV 疫苗接种政策、国际比较及成本效益;(6) 未来的研究重点,包括 OPC 预防、HPV 和男性不育,以及泌尿科特定感染控制指南的需求。从 2026 年起,韩国将把 12 岁男孩纳入国家免疫计划,这是韩国首个性别中立的 HPV 疫苗接种 政策。这篇综述强调了泌尿科医师在 HPV 管理中不断扩大且不可或缺的作用,并强调感染控制警惕和性别中立的 疫苗接种 策略对于减少 HPV 相关疾病日益增加的社会负担至关重要。本综述为泌尿科医生提供了一个实用的框架,将 HPV 预防、感染控制和 疫苗接种 咨询纳入常规临床实践。

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 本综述将人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)重新定位为泌尿外科、职业健康和公共卫生的重要问题。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 提供的证据中未报告具体的争议或证据缺口。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 从2026年起,韩国将在其国家免疫计划中纳入12岁男孩——这是韩国首个性别中立的人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)防控政策。

papers.title: Incidence and Prevalence of Human Papillomavirus Infection to Predict Outcomes from HPV-Based Cervical Cancer Screening in Women and People with a Cervix Living with HIV
papers.abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) testing has been implemented in many organized cervix screening programs; however, understanding how this screening methodology affects rates of colposcopy and further follow-up procedures remains underexplored, especially among women with HIV. In the absence of HPV screening program data in British Columbia (BC), Canada, we sought to determine HPV prevalence and estimates for colposcopies among a cohort of women with HIV using the BC Cervix Screening algorithm. Setting: HPV data were collected and analyzed from a prospective HPV vaccine immunogenicity cohort study of women with HIV from 14 sites of HIV care across Canada from 2008 to 2015. Methods: HPV data were obtained during the screening (month −3), baseline (month 0), month 12, and month 24 time points (Linear Array assay). Participant demographic and clinical characteristics (CD4 + count, HIV viral load, etc.) were assessed to determine associations between HPV prevalence and estimates for colposcopy using rate ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Results: Overall, 47.2% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening which would result in a colposcopy referral. In total, 15.9% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening, month 12, and month 24 time points, which would result in 3 consecutive referrals to colposcopy. Participants with repeat oncogenic HPV detected were less likely to have a suppressed HIV viral load compared with participants without oncogenic HPV detected. Conclusions: Results of this study suggest that HPV testing will result in a high proportion of referrals to colposcopy and follow-up procedures among women with HIV, which will require preparation and planning. Further work is needed to provide the appropriate support and education for women with HIV when incorporating HPV testing into cervix screening programs.
papers.journal: JAIDS Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to assess the impact of HPV testing on colposcopy referral rates among women with HIV in Canada. HPV data were collected from a prospective cohort study across 14 HIV care sites between 2008 and 2015. The Linear Array assay was used to detect oncogenic HPV at screening, baseline, and follow-up time points. Results showed that 47.2% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening, leading to colposcopy referrals, and 15.9% had persistent HPV infections over 24 months, resulting in three consecutive referrals. The authors suggest that these findings highlight the need for preparedness in cervical cancer screening programs for women with HIV, as HPV testing may significantly increase the demand for colposcopy and follow-up procedures. The study provides important insights into the implications of HPV screening in this population but does not report specific limitations or an evidence strength assessment.

papers.title_zh: 发病率 和 患病率 的 人乳头瘤病毒 感染可预测女性和宫颈 HIV 感染者基于 HPV 的 宫颈癌 筛查结果
papers.source_body_en: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) testing has been implemented in many organized cervix screening programs; however, understanding how this screening methodology affects rates of colposcopy and further follow-up procedures remains underexplored, especially among women with HIV. In the absence of HPV screening program data in British Columbia (BC), Canada, we sought to determine HPV prevalence and estimates for colposcopies among a cohort of women with HIV using the BC Cervix Screening algorithm. Setting: HPV data were collected and analyzed from a prospective HPV vaccine immunogenicity cohort study of women with HIV from 14 sites of HIV care across Canada from 2008 to 2015. Methods: HPV data were obtained during the screening (month −3), baseline (month 0), month 12, and month 24 time points (Linear Array assay). Participant demographic and clinical characteristics (CD4 + count, HIV viral load, etc.) were assessed to determine associations between HPV prevalence and estimates for colposcopy using rate ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Results: Overall, 47.2% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening which would result in a colposcopy referral. In total, 15.9% of participants had oncogenic HPV detected at screening, month 12, and month 24 time points, which would result in 3 consecutive referrals to colposcopy. Participants with repeat oncogenic HPV detected were less likely to have a suppressed HIV viral load compared with participants without oncogenic HPV detected. Conclusions: Results of this study suggest that HPV testing will result in a high proportion of referrals to colposcopy and follow-up procedures among women with HIV, which will require preparation and planning. Further work is needed to provide the appropriate support and education for women with HIV when incorporating HPV testing into cervix screening programs.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 检测已在许多有组织的子宫颈筛查计划中实施;然而,了解这种筛查方法如何影响阴道镜检查率和进一步的随访程序仍有待探索,特别是在感染艾滋病毒的女性中。由于加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省 (BC) 缺乏 HPV 筛查计划数据,我们试图使用 BC 子宫颈筛查算法确定感染 HIV 的 队列研究 女性中的 HPV 患病率 和阴道镜检查的估计值。背景:HPV 数据是从 2008 年至 2015 年加拿大 14 个 HIV 护理地点的 HIV 感染女性的前瞻性 HPV 疫苗 免疫原性 队列研究 研究中收集和分析的。方法:在筛查(第 -3 个月)、基线(第 0 个月)、第 12 个月和第 24 个月时间点(线性阵列测定)期间获得 HPV 数据。评估参与者的人口统计和临床特征(CD4 + 计数、HIV 病毒载量等),以确定 HPV 患病率 与使用比率和 95% 置信区间的阴道镜检查估计值之间的关联。结果:总体而言,47.2% 的参与者在筛查时检测到致癌 HPV,这将导致转诊阴道镜检查。总共有 15.9% 的参与者在筛查、第 12 个月和第 24 个月的时间点检测到致癌 HPV,这将导致连续 3 次转诊进行阴道镜检查。与未检测到致癌 HPV 的参与者相比,重复检测到致癌 HPV 的参与者 HIV 病毒载量受到抑制的可能性较小。结论:这项研究的结果表明,HPV 检测将导致 HIV 感染女性中较高比例的转诊到阴道镜检查和后续程序,这需要做好准备和规划。将 HPV 检测纳入子宫颈筛查计划时,需要开展进一步的工作,为感染艾滋病毒的女性提供适当的支持和教育。

papers.title: Micro-Costing Analysis for Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination Services for Out-of-School (OOS) Girls in Indonesia: Evidence from a Pilot Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Cervical cancer remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, with Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection responsible for nearly all cases. The government has integrated HPV vaccination into the national School Children Immunization Month (BIAS). However, out-of-school (OOS) girls remain difficult to reach because they are not covered by the school-based vaccination platform. This study aimed to estimate the cost of delivering a single-dose HPV vaccination program to OOS girls and to project the national-level cost of scaling up the program. Method: Micro-costing approach was used to estimate both economic and financial costs of delivering HPV vaccination to OOS girls in Bekasi City, Bandar Lampung City, and Bangka Regency. Costs were categorized into outreach and delivery efforts. A scale-up costing analysis was also conducted to estimate national-level costs. Result: The results show that the cost per vaccinated OOS girl aged 11 ranged from US$ 22.77 to 38.55, while the financial cost range from US$ 12.70 to 29.50, varied by implementation context, with outreach activities, transportation, and vaccine delivery supplies identified as the main cost drivers. The estimated national annual economic and financial cost of scaling-up HPV vaccination for OOS girls are US$ 644,215.23 and US$ 483,138.35, respectively. Conclusion: Optimizing OOS girls' outreach and HPV vaccination is essential to achieve sustained full coverage. National cost estimates show that reaching and vaccinating OOS girls accounts for less than 3% of the national immunization budget.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景:人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染是印度尼西亚宫颈癌的主要病因,而政府已将HPV疫苗接种纳入全国学校儿童免疫月(BIAS)。然而,非在校女生(OOS)由于未被学校平台覆盖,仍难以触及。本研究旨在估算向非在校女生提供单剂HPV疫苗接种计划的成本,并预测该计划在国家层面扩大规模后的成本。方法:采用微成本分析方法,估算在雅加达市、巴淡市和邦加县向非在校女生提供HPV疫苗接种计划的经济成本和财务成本。成本被分为外展和接种活动。还进行了扩大规模的成本分析,以估算国家层面的成本。结果:结果显示,11岁接种HPV疫苗的非在校女生每人成本范围为22.77至38.55美元,而财务成本范围为12.70至29.50美元,成本因实施背景而异,外展活动、交通和疫苗接种物资被确定为主要成本驱动因素。扩大HPV疫苗接种计划覆盖非在校女生的国家年度经济和财务成本估计分别为644,215.23美元和483,138.35美元。结论:优化非在校女生的外展和HPV疫苗接种对于实现持续全面覆盖至关重要。国家成本估算表明,接触和接种非在校女生仅占国家免疫预算的不到3%。
