papers.title: System Pharmacology Profiling of Plumbago zeylanica Linn. Against HPV-Associated Cervical Cancer
papers.abstract: Background: Cervical cancer remains a significant contributor to cancer-related deaths in women globally, with persistent infection by high-risk Human Papillomavirus (HPV) identified as its principal etiological driver. Aim: This study explored the mechanistic basis of Plumbago zeylanica’s potential anti-cervical cancer activity through a combined network pharmacology and molecular docking framework targeting HPV-associated pathogenic processes. Methods: Bioactive phytoconstituents of P. zeylanica were systematically compiled from published literature and the IMPPAT 2.0 database, then filtered through ADME criteria to retain compounds meeting drug-likeness thresholds. Putative protein targets for the shortlisted compounds were obtained via SwissTargetPrediction and SEA platforms, while genes linked to HPV-driven cervical carcinogenesis were sourced from the GeneCards repository using curated disease- and pathogen-specific search terms. Overlapping targets were mapped and used to construct a Protein–Protein Interaction (PPI) network, from which hub genes were identified through topological parameter analysis. Gene Ontology and pathway enrichment analyses were subsequently applied to delineate relevant biological processes, with emphasis on viral oncogenesis and immune-inflammatory signalling. Binding interactions between key phytoconstituents and prioritised hub proteins were then evaluated through molecular docking simulations. Results: Topological analysis of the PPI network highlighted JUN, NFKB1, IL1B, EGFR, and TNF as critical regulatory nodes within HPV-mediated oncogenic and inflammatory cascades. Pathway enrichment pointed to significant involvement of cancer-related pathways, TNF signalling, programmed cell death, immune checkpoint modulation, and viral infection mechanisms. Among the docked compounds, zeylanone emerged as the most promising candidate, displaying robust binding affinity toward JUN (−10.2 kcal/mol) and EGFR (−9.0 kcal/mol), while plumbagin, formononetin, diosmetin, and hispidulin also demonstrated favourable docking profiles against multiple targets. Conclusion: Collectively, these results indicate that Plumbago zeylanica may interfere with cervical cancer progression by simultaneously modulating several HPV-associated oncogenic signalling nodes. Nonetheless, rigorous in vitro and in vivo experimental validation remains essential to substantiate its clinical translational value. Major Findings: Network pharmacology study of Plumbago zeylanica identified JUN, NFKB1, IL1B, EGFR, and TNF as key targets involved in HPV-associated cervical cancer. Among the phytoconstituents, zeylanone exhibited the strongest multitarget binding affinity, followed by formononetin, diosmetin, hispidulin, and plumbagin. All had considerable multi-target interactions, which suggest a coordinated multi-component mechanism of action.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential anti-cervical cancer activity of Plumbago zeylanica through a network pharmacology and molecular docking approach, focusing on HPV-associated pathogenic processes. The research aimed to identify the mechanistic basis of its therapeutic effects by analyzing bioactive compounds and their interactions with key proteins involved in HPV-mediated oncogenesis and inflammation. The methods included compiling phytoconstituents, filtering them using ADME criteria, identifying protein targets via computational platforms, and constructing a PPI network to pinpoint critical regulatory nodes. The main results highlighted JUN, NFKB1, IL1B, EGFR, and TNF as key targets, with zeylanone showing the strongest binding affinity. The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that P. zeylanica may modulate multiple HPV-associated oncogenic pathways, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for cervical cancer. However, they emphasized the need for further experimental validation to confirm clinical relevance. The study contributes to understanding the molecular mechanisms of natural remedies against HPV-associated cervical cancer, offering insights for future research and drug development.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer remains a significant contributor to cancer-related deaths in women globally, with persistent infection by high-risk Human Papillomavirus (HPV) identified as its principal etiological driver.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This study explored the mechanistic basis of Plumbago zeylanica’s potential anti-cervical cancer activity through a combined network pharmacology and molecular docking framework targeting HPV-associated pathogenic processes.
analysis_en.methods: Bioactive phytoconstituents of P. zeylanica were systematically compiled from published literature and the IMPPAT 2.0 database, then filtered through ADME criteria to retain compounds meeting drug-likeness thresholds. Putative protein targets for the shortlisted compounds were obtained via SwissTargetPrediction and SEA platforms, while genes linked to HPV-driven cervical carcinogenesis were sourced from the GeneCards repository using curated disease- and pathogen-specific search terms. Overlapping targets were mapped and used to construct a Protein–Protein Interaction (PPI) network, from which hub genes were identified through topological parameter analysis.
analysis_en.main_results: Topological analysis of the PPI network highlighted JUN, NFKB1, IL1B, EGFR, and TNF as critical regulatory nodes within HPV-mediated oncogenic and inflammatory cascades. Pathway enrichment pointed to significant involvement of cancer-related pathways, TNF signalling, programmed cell death, immune checkpoint modulation, and viral infection mechanisms. Among the docked compounds, zeylanone emerged as the most promising candidate, displaying robust binding affinity toward JUN (−10.2 kcal/mol) and EGFR (−9.0 kcal/mol), while plumbagin, formononetin, diosmetin, and hispidulin also demonstrated favourable docking profiles against multiple targets.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: Collectively, these results indicate that Plumbago zeylanica may interfere with cervical cancer progression by simultaneously modulating several HPV-associated oncogenic signalling nodes.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that Plumbago zeylanica may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for HPV-associated cervical cancer by targeting key oncogenic and inflammatory pathways.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Nonetheless, rigorous in vitro and in vivo experimental validation remains essential to substantiate its clinical translational value.

papers.title_zh: Plumbago zeylanica Linn. 对 HPV 相关 宫颈癌 的系统药理学分析
papers.source_body_en: Background: Cervical cancer remains a significant contributor to cancer-related deaths in women globally, with persistent infection by high-risk Human Papillomavirus (HPV) identified as its principal etiological driver. Aim: This study explored the mechanistic basis of Plumbago zeylanica’s potential anti-cervical cancer activity through a combined network pharmacology and molecular docking framework targeting HPV-associated pathogenic processes. Methods: Bioactive phytoconstituents of P. zeylanica were systematically compiled from published literature and the IMPPAT 2.0 database, then filtered through ADME criteria to retain compounds meeting drug-likeness thresholds. Putative protein targets for the shortlisted compounds were obtained via SwissTargetPrediction and SEA platforms, while genes linked to HPV-driven cervical carcinogenesis were sourced from the GeneCards repository using curated disease- and pathogen-specific search terms. Overlapping targets were mapped and used to construct a Protein–Protein Interaction (PPI) network, from which hub genes were identified through topological parameter analysis. Gene Ontology and pathway enrichment analyses were subsequently applied to delineate relevant biological processes, with emphasis on viral oncogenesis and immune-inflammatory signalling. Binding interactions between key phytoconstituents and prioritised hub proteins were then evaluated through molecular docking simulations. Results: Topological analysis of the PPI network highlighted JUN, NFKB1, IL1B, EGFR, and TNF as critical regulatory nodes within HPV-mediated oncogenic and inflammatory cascades. Pathway enrichment pointed to significant involvement of cancer-related pathways, TNF signalling, programmed cell death, immune checkpoint modulation, and viral infection mechanisms. Among the docked compounds, zeylanone emerged as the most promising candidate, displaying robust binding affinity toward JUN (−10.2 kcal/mol) and EGFR (−9.0 kcal/mol), while plumbagin, formononetin, diosmetin, and hispidulin also demonstrated favourable docking profiles against multiple targets. Conclusion: Collectively, these results indicate that Plumbago zeylanica may interfere with cervical cancer progression by simultaneously modulating several HPV-associated oncogenic signalling nodes. Nonetheless, rigorous in vitro and in vivo experimental validation remains essential to substantiate its clinical translational value. Major Findings: Network pharmacology study of Plumbago zeylanica identified JUN, NFKB1, IL1B, EGFR, and TNF as key targets involved in HPV-associated cervical cancer. Among the phytoconstituents, zeylanone exhibited the strongest multitarget binding affinity, followed by formononetin, diosmetin, hispidulin, and plumbagin. All had considerable multi-target interactions, which suggest a coordinated multi-component mechanism of action.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:宫颈癌 仍是全球女性癌症相关死亡的重要原因,高危型 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)的持续感染被确定为其主要病因。目的:本研究通过结合网络药理学和分子对接框架,探讨 Plumbago zeylanica 对 HPV 相关 宫颈癌 潜在抗病毒作用的机制基础。方法:从已发表文献和 IMPPAT 2.0 数据库中系统性地收集 P. zeylanica 的生物活性成分,然后通过 ADME 标准筛选,保留符合药物样性阈值的化合物。通过 SwissTargetPrediction 和 SEA 平台获得短名单化合物的潜在蛋白质靶点,同时使用经过整理的疾病和病原体特异性搜索词从 GeneCards 仓库中获取与 HPV 驱动的宫颈癌相关的基因。重叠靶点被映射并用于构建蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用(PPI)网络,通过拓扑参数分析识别出枢纽基因。随后进行基因本体和通路富集分析,以明确相关生物过程,重点强调病毒致癌和免疫-炎症信号传导。最后,通过分子对接模拟评估关键植物成分与优先选择的枢纽蛋白之间的结合相互作用。结果:PPI 网络的拓扑分析突出了 JUN、NFKB1、IL1B、EGFR 和 TNF 作为 HPV 介导的致癌和炎症级联中的关键调控节点。通路富集分析表明,这些结果涉及癌症相关通路、TNF 信号传导、程序性细胞死亡、免疫检查点调节以及病毒感染机制。在对接的化合物中,泽兰酮(zeylanone)被确定为最有前景的候选物,显示出对 JUN(−10.2 kcal/mol)和 EGFR(−9.0 kcal/mol)的强结合亲和力,而漆姑草素(plumbagin)、芒柄花素(formononetin)、二氢山柰酚(diosmetin)和异鼠李素(hispidulin)也显示出对多个靶点的有利对接特征。结论:总体而言,这些结果表明 Plumbago zeylanica 可能通过同时调节多个与 HPV 相关的致癌信号节点来干扰 宫颈癌 的进展。然而,严格的体外和体内实验验证仍然是确立其临床转化价值所必需的。主要发现:Plumbago zeylanica 的网络药理学研究确定了 JUN、NFKB1、IL1B、EGFR 和 TNF 作为与 HPV 相关的 宫颈癌 关键靶点。在这些植物成分中,泽兰酮表现出最强的多靶点结合亲和力,其次是芒柄花素、二氢山柰酚、异鼠李素和漆姑草素。所有这些成分都显示出显著的多靶点相互作用,表明其可能通过协调的多组分机制发挥作用。

papers.title: A Gender-Oriented Approach to Human Papillomavirus Vaccination: A Cross-Sectional Study Among Preclinical Medical Students
papers.abstract: Objective: The first line of defense against cervical cancer is human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination. The perception that HPV vaccination is primarily intended for women hinders progress in the fight against HPV. This study aimed to examine preclinical medical students’ gender-based perspectives on the current HPV vaccination program and to assess the potential impact of gender-based approaches to cervical cancer prevention programs on their knowledge of HPV vaccination recommendations. Materials and Methods: This descriptive cross-sectional study assessed preclinical medical students’ awareness of HPV vaccination recommendations. The HPV Knowledge Scale was administered to eligible preclinical students. Incomplete questionnaires were excluded from the analysis. Results: A total of 448 questionnaires were analyzed, corresponding to an 88.3% response rate. Regarding the recommendation of the HPV vaccine for males aged 11–26 years, only 34.8% of male students (n=46) and 31.0% of female students (n=98) correctly identified this indication. For females aged 11–26 years, the proportion of correct responses was higher, at 60.6% (n=80) among male students and 69.3% (n=219) among female students. Conclusion: Improving medical students’ knowledge of vaccination programs is an important step toward achieving primary prevention, a key objective of public health practice. Our findings demonstrate that preclinical medical students have lower awareness of HPV vaccination recommendations for males than for females, indicating an urgent need to strengthen gender-neutral HPV vaccination content in undergraduate medical ­education.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 针对宫颈癌的第一道防线是人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)疫苗接种。本研究旨在探讨临床医学预科生对当前HPV 疫苗接种项目的性别视角,并评估基于性别的方法对宫颈癌预防项目对其HPV 疫苗接种建议知识的潜在影响。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 材料与方法:本描述性横断面研究评估了预临床医学学生的HPV 疫苗接种建议知晓情况。将HPV知识量表发放给符合条件的预临床学生。不完整的问卷被排除在分析之外。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 共分析了448份问卷,对应88.3%的回复率。关于推荐高危型HPV疫苗(疫苗)用于11–26岁男性,仅34.8%的男性学生(n=46)和31.0%的女性学生(n=98)正确识别了这一适应症。对于11–26岁女性,正确回答的比例更高,分别为60.6%(n=80)的男性学生和69.3%(n=219)的女性学生。提高医学生对疫苗接种项目的了解是实现一级预防的重要步骤,这是一公共卫生实践的关键目标。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 我们的研究结果表明,临床前医学学生对男性HPV 疫苗接种建议的知晓率低于对女性的知晓率,这表明亟需加强本科医学教育中性别中立的HPV 疫苗接种内容。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 认为人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 主要针对女性的观念阻碍了对抗 HPV 的进展。

papers.title: Human Papillomavirus (HPV)-Infected Epithelial Cells and FBLN1-Positive Fibroreticular Cells Govern the Immunogenic Tumor Microenvironment in HPV-Associated Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) exhibits distinct clinical behaviors according to human papillomavirus (HPV) status. HPV-associated OPSCC is typically associated with a more favorable prognosis and improved response to therapy than non-HPV–associated OPSCC; however, the underlying differences in the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain incompletely understood.Methods. To investigate cellular and molecular factors associated with improved outcomes in HPV-associated OPSCC, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing and high-resolution spatial transcriptomics on samples from two non-HPV–associated OPSCCs, five HPV-associated OPSCCs, and three normal tonsils, with a particular focus on fibroreticular cells (FRCs).Results. Four distinct FRC subsets were identified, with FBLN1-positive FRCs significantly enriched in HPV-associated OPSCC. These cells expressed SLIT2, a molecule implicated in immune cell recruitment. Spatial mapping demonstrated that FBLN1-positive FRCs were closely associated with both tumor and immune cells, suggesting a role in promoting an immunogenic TME. In addition, HPV-associated OPSCC exhibited higher levels of proliferating epithelial cells and increased expression of antigen-presentation genes than non-HPV–associated tumors.Conclusion. These findings highlight the potential role of FBLN1-positive FRCs in promoting immune activation within the TME of HPV-associated OPSCC. Enhanced antigen presentation and epithelial proliferation may facilitate tumor-immune interactions, potentially contributing to improved clinical outcomes. This study advances understanding of TME dynamics in OPSCC and may inform future therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract_zh: 口咽部鳞状细胞癌(OPSCC)根据人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)状态表现出不同的临床行为。与非HPV相关的OPSCC相比,HPV相关的OPSCC通常具有更佳的预后和更好的治疗反应;然而,肿瘤微环境(TME)中的潜在差异仍不完全清楚。方法:为了研究与HPV相关OPSCC改善预后相关的细胞和分子因素,我们对来自两例非HPV相关OPSCC、五例HPV相关OPSCC和三例正常扁桃体的样本进行了单细胞RNA测序和高分辨率空间转录组分析,特别关注纤维网状细胞(FRCs)。结果:识别出四种不同的FRC亚群,其中FBLN1阳性的FRCs在HPV相关OPSCC中显著富集。这些细胞表达SLIT2,这是一种与免疫细胞招募相关的分子。空间映射显示,FBLN1阳性的FRCs与肿瘤细胞和免疫细胞紧密相关,表明其在促进免疫原性TME中的作用。此外,HPV相关OPSCC表现出更高的上皮细胞增殖水平和抗原呈递基因表达增加。结论:这些发现突出了FBLN1阳性的FRCs在促进HPV相关OPSCC肿瘤微环境中的免疫激活的潜在作用。增强的抗原呈递和上皮增殖可能促进肿瘤-免疫相互作用,从而可能有助于改善临床结果。本研究推进了对OPSCC肿瘤微环境动态的理解,并可能为未来的治疗策略提供信息。

Topics & Projects Antimicrobial Stewardship Chronic Wasting Disease Osterholm Update Podcasts Newsletters About CIDRAP CIDRAP in the News Our Staff Our Director Osterholm in the Press Shop Merchandise Contact Us About Search CLOSE Search Support Menu HPV infection may confer slightly higher risk of new-onset heart disease and death News brief Mary Van Beusekom, MS Topics Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Share Copied to clipboard Chinnapong / iStock Women infected with human papillomavirus (HPV) are at higher risk for new-onset cardiovascular disease (CVD) and death than their uninfected peers, a Karolinska Institutet–led research team suggests. For the observational study, published yesterday in PLOS Medicine, the researchers compared the CVD diagnoses of 497,445 HPV-infected women in Swedish national registries with those of roughly 2.5 million uninfected controls. They also compared CVD status among 143,787 infected women and their 174,637 unexposed full siblings. The authors note that most previous observational research was limited to specific populations and didn’t adequately consider familial factors. HPV infection is well known to cause cervical cancer, but emerging evidence suggests that it may also contribute to CVD. Sibling comparison yields similar findings New-onset CVD was identified in 28,793 and 128,373 HPV-infected and uninfected women, respectively, for respective incidences of 8.27 and 7.93 per 1,000 person-years. In total, 1,221 and 4,941 women with and without HPV infection died of CVD, for respective death rates of 33.7 and 29.4 per 100,000 person-years. The risks of CVD and death were greatest within the first year of follow-up, then waned. The findings suggested that clinicians should be aware of a slightly elevated CVD risk in women with HPV, especially during the first year following an infection. The risk of new-onset CVD was 7% higher in HPV-infected women than in their uninfected counterparts, for an absolute rate difference of 0.53 cases per 1,000 person-years (population-attributable fraction, 1.16%). The risk of death was 25% higher in infected women than in unexposed women, for an absolute rate difference of 6.71 cases per 100,000 person-years (population-attributable fraction, 4.12%). In the first year of follow-up, the risks of incident CVD and related death were 43% and 86% higher, respectively, in women diagnosed as having HPV. But thereafter, the excess risk fell to 2% for new-onset CVD and 21% for related death. In the sibling comparison, HPV-infected women had a 5% greater risk of incident CVD and a 25% higher risk of death than their uninfected siblings. “The findings suggested that clinicians should be aware of a slightly elevated CVD risk in women with HPV, especially during the first year following an infection,” the authors concluded. “However, given the small absolute difference, women should not be unduly concerned.” Monoclonal antibody shows promise against dengue viremia, fever in phase 2 trial News brief Chris Dall, MA Topics Dengue Monica R / Flickr cc An experimental monoclonal antibody (mAb) for dengue virus was safe and well-tolerated and provided evidence of a therapeutic effect in a phase 2 clinical trial, researchers reported last week in JAMA Network Open. In the randomized, placebo-controlled trial, a team led by investigators from Serum Institute of India assigned 250 adults with dengue and a history of fever onset within 48 hours to receive four different dose levels of Dengue-mAb (3, 5, 7, or 9 milligrams per kilogram [mg/kg]) or a placebo, with 50 participants assigned to each group. The primary outcomes were reduction in viremia at 24 hours and causally related serious adverse events (SAEs). Dengue-mAb is a human-engineered, recombinant monoclonal antibody that has neutralized all four serotypes of dengue virus in animal studies and demonstrated safety in a phase 1 trial in healthy adults. Dengue virus affects more than 200 million people each year and is expanding into new areas amid climate change and rapid urbanization. In addition, the incidence of severe disease from the fast-spreading mosquito-borne virus is rising. While there are three currently licensed vaccines for dengue, there are no licensed antiviral drugs. “Improvements in case management to reduce the risk of severe dengue are still needed,” the investigators wrote. Rapid clearance of viremia, fever Treatment with Dengue-mAb demonstrated a rapid clearance of dengue viremia and fever within 24 hours at all dose levels compared with placebo. Participants with detectable viremia at baseline were negative for dengue virus by eight hours when treated with the 5- to 9-mg/kg dose of Dengue-mAb, compared with 72 hours with placebo. At 24 hours, fever clearance ranged from 92.9% to 100% in the Dengue-mAb groups, compared with 58.3% in the placebo group. This is, to our knowledge, the first evidence of a preliminary therapeutic effect in patients with dengue. No causally related SAEs were recorded. “This first-in-patient phase 2 randomized clinical trial demonstrated the safety of Dengue-mAb and its action on the clearance of dengue virus and fever,” the authors wrote. “This is, to our knowledge, the first evidence of a preliminary therapeutic effect in patients with dengue.” In case you missed it Previous Next Quick takes: Cyclosporiasis in Michigan, Aedes mosquitoes in the UK, new NYC Legionnaires measures Regular exercise before COVID infection linked to better daily function 2 years later Study details deaths, anaphylaxis linked to antibiotic injections Ebola case counts reach 6,250 in DR Congo outbreak Lancaster County coroner confirms that second measles death also involves a child Rotavirus vaccine shows strong global results in preschoolers Antiviral drug remdesivir may cut risk of death in adults with severe COVID and kidney or liver disease Quick takes: Schools resume in DR Congo; sprouts, mangos recalled; 2 H9N2 avian flu cases in China This week's top reads Newborn one of 2 measles-associated deaths in Pennsylvania The baby died of a laceration of the spleen, which may have been caused by a measles infection in the mother. analysis.time: The study was published on 2026-09-02, and the findings were based on data from Swedish national registries and follow-up periods up to one year post-infection.
analysis.location_and_population: The study focused on women in Sweden, comparing those infected with HPV with uninfected controls and their unexposed full siblings.
analysis.event: A research study published in PLOS Medicine suggests that HPV infection may confer a slightly higher risk of new-onset cardiovascular disease (CVD) and death, particularly within the first year of follow-up.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The risk of new-onset CVD was 7% higher in HPV-infected women than in uninfected counterparts, with an absolute rate difference of 0.53 cases per 1,000 person-years. The risk of death was 25% higher in infected women, with an absolute rate difference of 6.71 cases per 100,000 person-years. In the first year, the risks were 43% and 86% higher for CVD and death, respectively, but declined afterward.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study is observational and highlights the need for clinicians to be aware of the slightly elevated CVD risk in women with HPV, especially during the first year post-infection. The authors note that the small absolute difference means women should not be unduly concerned. The findings are based on Swedish registries and sibling comparisons, with no causally related serious adverse events recorded.

analysis.brief_en: A study published in PLOS Medicine suggests that HPV infection may slightly increase the risk of new-onset cardiovascular disease (CVD) and death in women, particularly within the first year of infection. The research, led by Karolinska Institutet, compared 497,445 HPV-infected women with 2.5 million uninfected controls and found a 7% higher risk of CVD and a 25% higher risk of death in infected women. In the first year, the risks were 43% and 86% higher, respectively, but declined afterward. The study also compared 143,787 infected women with their 174,637 unexposed siblings, yielding similar results. The authors advise clinicians to be aware of the slightly elevated CVD risk in HPV-infected women but emphasize that the small absolute difference does not warrant undue concern. No serious adverse events were recorded, and the findings are based on Swedish national registries.

analysis_en.time: The study was published on 2026-09-02, and the findings were based on data from Swedish national registries and follow-up periods up to one year post-infection.
analysis_en.location_and_population: The study focused on women in Sweden, comparing those infected with HPV with uninfected controls and their unexposed full siblings.
analysis_en.event: A research study published in PLOS Medicine suggests that HPV infection may confer a slightly higher risk of new-onset cardiovascular disease (CVD) and death, particularly within the first year of follow-up.
analysis_en.scale_impact_and_risk: The risk of new-onset CVD was 7% higher in HPV-infected women than in uninfected counterparts, with an absolute rate difference of 0.53 cases per 1,000 person-years. The risk of death was 25% higher in infected women, with an absolute rate difference of 6.71 cases per 100,000 person-years. In the first year, the risks were 43% and 86% higher for CVD and death, respectively, but declined afterward.
analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study is observational and highlights the need for clinicians to be aware of the slightly elevated CVD risk in women with HPV, especially during the first year post-infection. The authors note that the small absolute difference means women should not be unduly concerned. The findings are based on Swedish registries and sibling comparisons, with no causally related serious adverse events recorded.

news.title_zh: HPV感染可能略微增加新发心脏病和死亡风险
news.source_body_en: A study published in PLOS Medicine suggests that HPV infection may slightly increase the risk of new-onset cardiovascular disease (CVD) and death in women, particularly within the first year of infection. The research, led by Karolinska Institutet, compared 497,445 HPV-infected women with 2.5 million uninfected controls and found a 7% higher risk of CVD and a 25% higher risk of death in infected women. In the first year, the risks were 43% and 86% higher, respectively, but declined afterward. The study also compared 143,787 infected women with their 174,637 unexposed siblings, yielding similar results. The authors advise clinicians to be aware of the slightly elevated CVD risk in HPV-infected women but emphasize that the small absolute difference does not warrant undue concern. No serious adverse events were recorded, and the findings are based on Swedish national registries.

A smaller percentage of adolescents received the HPV series compared with recipients of the tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis (whooping cough) vaccine (Tdap) and the conjugate meningococcal vaccine against the A, C, W, and Y strains (Men ACWY). But uptake of these immunizations declined slightly from last year. “The consistently lower HPV vaccination coverage compared with other routine adolescent vaccines might, in part, reflect differences in school entry requirements,” wrote the authors, from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). “Tdap is required for school entry in all states, and MenACWY is required in most states; however, few states require HPV vaccination.” Need to address barriers to vaccination The researchers examined data from the 2025 National Immunization Survey–Teen to understand vaccination rates in teens aged 13 to 17 years. Children aged 11 to 12 should receive a Tdap, MenACWY, and HPV vaccine (though the HPV series can be started at 9 years old), per the 2025 CDC Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule. Last year, the number of teens aged 13 to 17 who received at least one dose each of Tdap and MenACWY dropped from 2024. For Tdap, the percentage of teens receiving at least one dose declined from 91.3% to 88.8%. When it came to MenACWY, the percentage dipped from 90.1% to 89.0%. While the recent survey stated the number of teens receiving the HPV vaccine held steady from the previous four years, it did not include those data. But last year’s survey, which reflects vaccine coverage data for 2024, showed that 78.2% of teens aged 13 to 17 received one dose or more of the HPV vaccine, and 62.9% completed the series. Efforts to address barriers to vaccination, including improving access to preventive care, strengthening provider communication regarding recommendations, and increasing vaccine confidence, could help improve coverage. In 2025, 63.4% of teens in the same age-group received the entire HPV vaccine series, far lower than the Healthy People 2030 goal of 80% being fully vaccinated. And the portion receiving at least one dose dropped by a half percentage point from the year before, to 77.7%. The percentage of teens 13 to 17 who received both doses of the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine (MMR) vaccine was 92.5%, also lower than the 95% Healthy People 2030 goal. “Continued efforts are needed to increase adolescent vaccination coverage with recommended vaccines and reduce geographic differences in coverage, particularly with HPV vaccine,” the authors wrote. “Efforts to address barriers to vaccination, including improving access to preventive care, strengthening provider communication regarding recommendations, and increasing vaccine confidence, could help improve coverage.” Related news Previous Next Vaccine recommendations and access, plus measles deaths: 3 questions, zero consensus: The State of US Vaccine Policy Izzy Brandstetter Figueroa, PhD, MPH, Riley Mulholland, MPH, Jess Steier, DrPH About one-third of US women in their 20s have never been screened for cervical cancer Meghan Holohan Newborn one of 2 measles-associated deaths in Pennsylvania Sarah Boden Studies provide more evidence that HPV vaccines benefit men Liz Szabo CIDRAP Op-Ed: What a package insert actually says, and how it was turned against vaccines Jake Scott, MD Catholic bishops tell Florida AG there's no theological reason for school vaccine exemptions Sarah Boden People vaccinated against HPV have lower risk of head and neck cancer, study suggests Liz Szabo CIDRAP Op-Ed: No, 3 vaccines are not better than 1 when it comes to MMR Jess Steier, DrPh This week's top reads Newborn one of 2 measles-associated deaths in Pennsylvania The baby died of a laceration of the spleen, which may have been caused by a measles infection in the mother. news.title_original: HPV vaccine uptake in US teens hasn’t increased in 4 years

analysis.time: The report states that the HPV vaccine uptake in US teens has not increased in 4 years, with data reflecting 2024 coverage. The survey data for 2025 was also mentioned, but the decline in Tdap and MenACWY was noted for 2024 compared to 2023. The publication date is 2026-09-04.
analysis.location_and_population: The report focuses on the United States, specifically on teenagers aged 13 to 17 years. It also references the broader population of US women in their 20s and the general public in Pennsylvania.
analysis.event: The event is the lack of increase in HPV vaccine uptake among US teenagers over the past four years, as reported in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. The CDC authors noted that the lower HPV vaccination coverage compared to other routine adolescent vaccines might be due to differences in school entry requirements.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: In 2024, 78.2% of US teens aged 13 to 17 received at least one dose of the HPV vaccine, and 62.9% completed the series. The percentage of teens receiving both doses of the MMR vaccine was 92.5%, which is lower than the Healthy People 2030 goal of 95%. The report highlights the need for continued efforts to improve coverage, especially for HPV.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The CDC authors suggest addressing barriers to vaccination, such as improving access to preventive care, strengthening provider communication, and increasing vaccine confidence. The report also mentions the Healthy People 2030 goals and the need for continued efforts to increase vaccination rates.

analysis.brief_en: The report highlights that HPV vaccine uptake among US teenagers aged 13 to 17 has not increased over the past four years. According to the 2025 National Immunization Survey–Teen, 78.2% of teens received at least one dose of the HPV vaccine, and 62.9% completed the series. This is lower than the Healthy People 2030 goal of 80% full vaccination. The CDC authors suggest that the lower coverage might be due to fewer states requiring HPV vaccination compared to Tdap and MenACWY vaccines. They recommend addressing barriers to vaccination, including improving access to preventive care, strengthening provider communication, and increasing vaccine confidence. The report also notes that the percentage of teens receiving both doses of the MMR vaccine was 92.5%, below the 95% Healthy People 2030 target. These findings underscore the need for continued efforts to enhance HPV vaccination rates among adolescents.

They recommend addressing barriers to vaccination, including improving access to preventive care, strengthening provider communication, and increasing vaccine confidence. The report also notes that the percentage of teens receiving both doses of the MMR vaccine was 92.5%, below the 95% Healthy People 2030 target. These findings underscore the need for continued efforts to enhance HPV vaccination rates among adolescents.
